rules.title: LSASS Process Crashed - Application
rules.description:
Detects Windows error reporting events where the process that crashed is LSASS (Local Security Authority Subsystem Service).
This could be the cause of a provoked crash by techniques such as Lsass-Shtinkering to dump credentials.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Rare legitimate crashing of the lsass process

rules.title: Microsoft Malware Protection Engine Crash
rules.description: This rule detects a suspicious crash of the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: MsMpEng might crash if the "C:\" partition is full

rules.title: Dump Ntds.dit To Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects potential abuse of ntdsutil to dump ntds.dit database to a suspicious location
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Ntdsutil Abuse
rules.description: Detects potential abuse of ntdsutil to dump ntds.dit database
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Backup Catalog Deleted
rules.description: Detects backup catalog deletions
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tom U. @c_APT_ure (collection)

rules.title: Restricted Software Access By SRP
rules.description: Detects restricted access to applications by the Software Restriction Policies (SRP) policy
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Audit CVE Event
rules.description:
Detects events generated by user-mode applications when they call the CveEventWrite API when a known vulnerability is trying to be exploited.
MS started using this log in Jan. 2020 with CVE-2020-0601 (a Windows CryptoAPI vulnerability.
Unfortunately, that is about the only instance of CVEs being written to this log.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Zach Mathis

rules.title: Application Uninstalled
rules.description: An application has been removed. Check if it is critical.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: MSI Installation From Suspicious Locations
rules.description: Detects MSI package installation from suspicious locations
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: False positives may occur if you allow installation from folders such as the desktop, the public folder or remote shares. A baseline is required before production use.

rules.title: MSI Installation From Web
rules.description: Detects installation of a remote msi file from web.
rules.author: Stamatis Chatzimangou

rules.title: Atera Agent Installation
rules.description: Detects successful installation of Atera Remote Monitoring & Management (RMM) agent as recently found to be used by Conti operators
rules.author: Bhabesh Raj

rules.title: MSSQL Add Account To Sysadmin Role
rules.description: Detects when an attacker tries to backdoor the MSSQL server by adding a backdoor account to the sysadmin fixed server role
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: MSSQL Destructive Query
rules.description: Detects the invocation of MS SQL transactions that are destructive towards table or database data, such as "DROP TABLE" or "DROP DATABASE".
rules.author: Daniel Degasperi '@d4ns4n_'

rules.title: MSSQL Disable Audit Settings
rules.description: Detects when an attacker calls the "ALTER SERVER AUDIT" or "DROP SERVER AUDIT" transaction in order to delete or disable audit logs on the server
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: This event should only fire when an administrator is modifying the audit policy. Which should be a rare occurrence once it's set up

rules.title: MSSQL Server Failed Logon From External Network
rules.description: Detects failed logon attempts from clients with external network IP to an MSSQL server. This can be a sign of a bruteforce attack.
rules.author: j4son

rules.title: MSSQL Server Failed Logon
rules.description: Detects failed logon attempts from clients to MSSQL server.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), j4son
falsepositives: This event could stem from users changing an account's password that's used to authenticate via a job or an automated process. Investigate the source of such events and mitigate them

rules.title: MSSQL SPProcoption Set
rules.description: Detects when the a stored procedure is set or cleared for automatic execution in MSSQL. A stored procedure that is set to automatic execution runs every time an instance of SQL Server is started
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the feature by administrators (rare)

rules.title: MSSQL XPCmdshell Suspicious Execution
rules.description: Detects when the MSSQL "xp_cmdshell" stored procedure is used to execute commands
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: MSSQL XPCmdshell Option Change
rules.description: Detects when the MSSQL "xp_cmdshell" stored procedure setting is changed.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Note that since the event contain the change for both values. This means that this will trigger on both enable and disable

rules.title: Relevant Anti-Virus Signature Keywords In Application Log
rules.description: Detects potentially highly relevant antivirus events in the application log based on known virus signature names and malware keywords.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Arnim Rupp
falsepositives: Some software piracy tools (key generators, cracks) are classified as hack tools

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Command Execution
rules.description: Detects command execution via ScreenConnect RMM
rules.author: Ali Alwashali

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect File Transfer
rules.description: Detects file being transferred via ScreenConnect RMM
rules.author: Ali Alwashali

rules.title: Microsoft Malware Protection Engine Crash - WER
rules.description: This rule detects a suspicious crash of the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: MsMpEng might crash if the "C:\" partition is full

rules.title: AppLocker Prevented Application or Script from Running
rules.description: Detects when AppLocker prevents the execution of an Application, DLL, Script, MSI, or Packaged-App from running.
rules.author: Pushkarev Dmitry
falsepositives: Unlikely, since this event notifies about blocked application execution. Tune your applocker rules to avoid blocking legitimate applications.

rules.title: AppLocker Application Would Have Been Blocked
rules.description: Detects when AppLocker "Audit only" enforcement mode reports that an Application, DLL, Script, MSI, or Packaged-App would have been blocked if AppLocker "Enforce rules" enforcement mode was enabled.
rules.author: heyyanu
falsepositives: Expected during AppLocker policy testing and audit mode deployments

rules.title: Sysinternals Tools AppX Versions Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of Sysinternals tools via an AppX package.
Attackers could install the Sysinternals Suite to get access to tools such as psexec and procdump to avoid detection based on System paths.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of sysinternals applications from the Windows Store will trigger this. Apply exclusions as needed.

rules.title: Deployment AppX Package Was Blocked By AppLocker
rules.description: Detects an appx package deployment that was blocked by AppLocker policy.
rules.author: frack113
falsepositives: Unlikely, since this event notifies about blocked application deployment. Tune your applocker rules to avoid blocking legitimate applications.

rules.title: Remote AppX Package Downloaded from File Sharing or CDN Domain
rules.description: Detects an appx package that was added to the pipeline of the "to be processed" packages which was downloaded from a file sharing or CDN domain.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Unlikely, unless the organization uses file sharing or CDN services to distribute internal applications.

rules.title: AppX Package Deployment Failed Due to Signing Requirements
rules.description: Detects an appx package deployment / installation with the error code "0x80073cff" which indicates that the package didn't meet the signing requirements.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate AppX packages not signed by MS used part of an enterprise.

rules.title: AppX Located in Known Staging Directory Added to Deployment Pipeline
rules.description: Detects an appx package that was added to the pipeline of the "to be processed" packages that is located in a known folder often used as a staging directory.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Malicious AppX Package Installation Attempts
rules.description: Detects potential installation or installation attempts of known malicious appx packages
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Rare occasions where a malicious package uses the exact same name and version as a legitimate application.

rules.title: Deployment Of The AppX Package Was Blocked By The Policy
rules.description:
Detects an appx package deployment that was blocked by the local computer policy.
The following events indicate that an AppX package deployment was blocked by a policy:
- Event ID 441: The package deployment operation is blocked by the "Allow deployment operations in special profiles" policy
- Event ID 442: Deployments to non-system volumes are blocked by the "Disable deployment of Windows Store apps to non-system volumes" policy."
- Event ID 453: Package blocked by a platform policy.
- Event ID 454: Package blocked by a platform policy.
rules.author: frack113
falsepositives: Unlikely, since this event notifies about blocked application deployment. Tune your applocker rules to avoid blocking legitimate applications.

rules.title: AppX Located in Uncommon Directory Added to Deployment Pipeline
rules.description: Detects an appx package that was added to the pipeline of the "to be processed" packages that is located in uncommon locations.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Windows AppX Deployment Full Trust Package Installation
rules.description: Detects the installation of MSIX/AppX packages with full trust privileges which run with elevated privileges outside normal AppX container restrictions
rules.author: Michael Haag, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Some legitimate applications installation which have been missed from filtering can generate fps, thus baselining and tuning is recommended before deploying to production

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Windows AppX Deployment Unsigned Package Installation
rules.description: Detects attempts to install unsigned MSIX/AppX packages using the -AllowUnsigned parameter via AppXDeployment-Server events
rules.author: Michael Haag, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate installation of unsigned packages for legitimate purposes such as development or testing

rules.title: Suspicious Digital Signature Of AppX Package
rules.description: Detects execution of AppX packages with known suspicious or malicious signature
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

selection.subjectName: CN=Foresee Consulting Inc., O=Foresee Consulting Inc., L=North York, S=Ontario, C=CA, SERIALNUMBER=1004913-1, OID.1.3.6.1.4.1.311.60.2.1.3=CA, OID.2.5.4.15=Private Organization

rules.title: New BITS Job Created Via Bitsadmin
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new bits job by Bitsadmin
rules.author: frack113
falsepositives: Many legitimate applications or scripts could leverage "bitsadmin". This event is best correlated with EID 16403 via the JobID field

rules.title: New BITS Job Created Via PowerShell
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new bits job by PowerShell
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: BITS Transfer Job Downloading File Potential Suspicious Extension
rules.description: Detects new BITS transfer job saving local files with potential suspicious extensions
rules.author: frack113
falsepositives: While the file extensions in question can be suspicious at times. It's best to add filters according to your environment to avoid large amount false positives

rules.title: BITS Transfer Job Download From File Sharing Domains
rules.description: Detects BITS transfer job downloading files from a file sharing domain.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: BITS Transfer Job Download From Direct IP
rules.description: Detects a BITS transfer job downloading file(s) from a direct IP address.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: BITS Transfer Job With Uncommon Or Suspicious Remote TLD
rules.description: Detects a suspicious download using the BITS client from a FQDN that is unusual. Adversaries may abuse BITS jobs to persistently execute or clean up after malicious payloads.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: This rule doesn't exclude other known TLDs such as ".org" or ".net". It's recommended to apply additional filters for software and scripts that leverage the BITS service

rules.title: BITS Transfer Job Download To Potential Suspicious Folder
rules.description: Detects new BITS transfer job where the LocalName/Saved file is stored in a potentially suspicious location
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Certificate Private Key Acquired
rules.description: Detects when an application acquires a certificate private key
rules.author: Zach Mathis
falsepositives: Legitimate application requesting certificate exports will trigger this. Apply additional filters as needed

rules.title: Certificate Exported From Local Certificate Store
rules.description: Detects when an application exports a certificate (and potentially the private key as well) from the local Windows certificate store.
rules.author: Zach Mathis
falsepositives: Legitimate application requesting certificate exports will trigger this. Apply additional filters as needed

rules.title: CodeIntegrity - Unmet Signing Level Requirements By File Under Validation
rules.description:
Detects attempted file load events that did not meet the signing level requirements. It often means the file's signature is revoked or a signature with the Lifetime Signing EKU has expired.
This event is best correlated with EID 3089 to determine the error of the validation.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Antivirus and other third party products are known to trigger this rule quite a lot. Initial filters and tuning is required before using this rule.

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: CodeIntegrity - Disallowed File For Protected Processes Has Been Blocked
rules.description: Detects block events for files that are disallowed by code integrity for protected processes
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: CodeIntegrity - Blocked Image/Driver Load For Policy Violation
rules.description: Detects blocked load events that did not meet the authenticode signing level requirements or violated the code integrity policy.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: CodeIntegrity - Blocked Driver Load With Revoked Certificate
rules.description: Detects blocked load attempts of revoked drivers
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: CodeIntegrity - Revoked Kernel Driver Loaded
rules.description: Detects the load of a revoked kernel driver
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: CodeIntegrity - Blocked Image Load With Revoked Certificate
rules.description: Detects blocked image load events with revoked certificates by code integrity.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: CodeIntegrity - Revoked Image Loaded
rules.description: Detects image load events with revoked certificates by code integrity.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: CodeIntegrity - Unsigned Kernel Module Loaded
rules.description: Detects the presence of a loaded unsigned kernel module on the system.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: CodeIntegrity - Unsigned Image Loaded
rules.description: Detects loaded unsigned image on the system
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: CodeIntegrity - Unmet WHQL Requirements For Loaded Kernel Module
rules.description: Detects loaded kernel modules that did not meet the WHQL signing requirements.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Loading Diagcab Package From Remote Path
rules.description: Detects loading of diagcab packages from a remote path, as seen in DogWalk vulnerability
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate package hosted on a known and authorized remote location

rules.title: DNS Query for Anonfiles.com Domain - DNS Client
rules.description: Detects DNS queries for anonfiles.com, which is an anonymous file upload platform often used for malicious purposes
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Cobalt Strike DNS Beaconing - DNS Client
rules.description: Detects a program that invoked suspicious DNS queries known from Cobalt Strike beacons
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DNS Query To MEGA Hosting Website - DNS Client
rules.description: Detects DNS queries for subdomains related to MEGA sharing website
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate DNS queries and usage of Mega

rules.title: DNS Query To Put.io - DNS Client
rules.description: Detects DNS queries for subdomains related to "Put.io" sharing website.
rules.author: Omar Khaled (@beacon_exe)
falsepositives: Legitimate DNS queries and usage of Put.io

rules.title: Query Tor Onion Address - DNS Client
rules.description: Detects DNS resolution of an .onion address related to Tor routing networks
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DNS Query To Ufile.io - DNS Client
rules.description: Detects DNS queries to "ufile.io", which was seen abused by malware and threat actors as a method for data exfiltration
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: DNS queries for "ufile" are not malicious by nature necessarily. Investigate the source to determine the necessary actions to take

rules.title: Failed DNS Zone Transfer
rules.description: Detects when a DNS zone transfer failed.
rules.author: Zach Mathis

rules.title: DNS Server Error Failed Loading the ServerLevelPluginDLL
rules.description: Detects a DNS server error in which a specified plugin DLL (in registry) could not be loaded
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: USB Device Plugged
rules.description: Detects plugged/unplugged USB devices
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: New Firewall Rule Added In Windows Firewall Exception List For Potential Suspicious Application
rules.description: Detects the addition of a new rule to the Windows Firewall exception list for an application located in a potentially suspicious location.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: New Firewall Rule Added In Windows Firewall Exception List Via WmiPrvSE.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the addition of a new "Allow" firewall rule by the WMI process (WmiPrvSE.EXE).
This can occur if an attacker leverages PowerShell cmdlets such as "New-NetFirewallRule", or directly uses WMI CIM classes such as "MSFT_NetFirewallRule".
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon New Firewall Rule Added In Windows Firewall Exception List
rules.description: Detects when a rule has been added to the Windows Firewall exception list
rules.author: frack113

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: All Rules Have Been Deleted From The Windows Firewall Configuration
rules.description: Detects when a all the rules have been deleted from the Windows Defender Firewall configuration
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: A Rule Has Been Deleted From The Windows Firewall Exception List
rules.description: Detects when a single rules or all of the rules have been deleted from the Windows Defender Firewall
rules.author: frack113

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: The Windows Defender Firewall Service Failed To Load Group Policy
rules.description: Detects activity when The Windows Defender Firewall service failed to load Group Policy
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Windows Defender Firewall Has Been Reset To Its Default Configuration
rules.description: Detects activity when Windows Defender Firewall has been reset to its default configuration
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Windows Firewall Settings Have Been Changed
rules.description: Detects activity when the settings of the Windows firewall have been changed
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: ETW Logging/Processing Option Disabled On IIS Server
rules.description: Detects changes to of the IIS server configuration in order to disable/remove the ETW logging/processing option.
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: HTTP Logging Disabled On IIS Server
rules.description: Detects changes to of the IIS server configuration in order to disable HTTP logging for successful requests.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: New Module Module Added To IIS Server
rules.description: Detects the addition of a new module to an IIS server.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Previously Installed IIS Module Was Removed
rules.description: Detects the removal of a previously installed IIS module.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: Potential Active Directory Reconnaissance/Enumeration Via LDAP
rules.description: Detects potential Active Directory enumeration via LDAP
rules.author: Adeem Mawani

detection.condition: (generic_search and not narrow_down_filter) or suspicious_flag or distinguished_name_enumeration

rules.title: Standard User In High Privileged Group
rules.description: Detect standard users login that are part of high privileged groups such as the Administrator group
rules.author: frack113
falsepositives: Standard domain users who are part of the administrator group. These users shouldn't have these right. But in the case where it's necessary. They should be filtered out using the "TargetUserName" field

rules.title: ProxyLogon MSExchange OabVirtualDirectory
rules.description: Detects specific patterns found after a successful ProxyLogon exploitation in relation to a Commandlet invocation of Set-OabVirtualDirectory
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Certificate Request Export to Exchange Webserver
rules.description: Detects a write of an Exchange CSR to an untypical directory or with aspx name suffix which can be used to place a webshell
rules.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Mailbox Export to Exchange Webserver
rules.description: Detects a successful export of an Exchange mailbox to untypical directory or with aspx name suffix which can be used to place a webshell or the needed role assignment for it
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Rich Warren, Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Remove Exported Mailbox from Exchange Webserver
rules.description: Detects removal of an exported Exchange mailbox which could be to cover tracks from ProxyShell exploit
rules.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Exchange Set OabVirtualDirectory ExternalUrl Property
rules.description: Rule to detect an adversary setting OabVirtualDirectory External URL property to a script in Exchange Management log
rules.author: Jose Rodriguez @Cyb3rPandaH

rules.title: Failed MSExchange Transport Agent Installation
rules.description: Detects a failed installation of a Exchange Transport Agent
rules.author: Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate installations of exchange TransportAgents. AssemblyPath is a good indicator for this.

rules.title: MSExchange Transport Agent Installation - Builtin
rules.description: Detects the Installation of a Exchange Transport Agent
rules.author: Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate installations of exchange TransportAgents. AssemblyPath is a good indicator for this.

rules.title: NTLM Logon
rules.description: Detects logons using NTLM, which could be caused by a legacy source or attackers
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: NTLM Brute Force
rules.description: Detects common NTLM brute force device names
rules.author: Jerry Shockley '@jsh0x'
falsepositives: Systems with names equal to the spoofed ones used by the brute force tools

rules.title: Potential Remote Desktop Connection to Non-Domain Host
rules.description: Detects logons using NTLM to hosts that are potentially not part of the domain.
rules.author: James Pemberton
falsepositives: Host connections to valid domains, exclude these.
Host connections not using host FQDN.
Host connections to external legitimate domains.

rules.title: OpenSSH Server Listening On Socket
rules.description: Detects scenarios where an attacker enables the OpenSSH server and server starts to listening on SSH socket.
rules.author: mdecrevoisier

rules.title: Potential Access Token Abuse
rules.description: Detects potential token impersonation and theft. Example, when using "DuplicateToken(Ex)" and "ImpersonateLoggedOnUser" with the "LOGON32_LOGON_NEW_CREDENTIALS flag".
rules.author: Michaela Adams, Zach Mathis

rules.title: Admin User Remote Logon
rules.description: Detect remote login by Administrator user (depending on internal pattern).
rules.author: juju4

rules.title: DiagTrackEoP Default Login Username
rules.description: Detects the default "UserName" used by the DiagTrackEoP POC
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: A Member Was Added to a Security-Enabled Global Group
rules.description: Detects activity when a member is added to a security-enabled global group
rules.author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime

rules.title: A Member Was Removed From a Security-Enabled Global Group
rules.description: Detects activity when a member is removed from a security-enabled global group
rules.author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime

rules.title: Successful Overpass the Hash Attempt
rules.description: Detects successful logon with logon type 9 (NewCredentials) which matches the Overpass the Hash behavior of e.g Mimikatz's sekurlsa::pth module.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (source), Dominik Schaudel (rule)

rules.title: Pass the Hash Activity 2
rules.description: Detects the attack technique pass the hash which is used to move laterally inside the network
rules.author: Dave Kennedy, Jeff Warren (method) / David Vassallo (rule)

rules.title: RDP Login from Localhost
rules.description: RDP login with localhost source address may be a tunnelled login
rules.author: Thomas Patzke

rules.title: A Security-Enabled Global Group Was Deleted
rules.description: Detects activity when a security-enabled global group is deleted
rules.author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime

rules.title: External Remote RDP Logon from Public IP
rules.description: Detects successful logon from public IP address via RDP. This can indicate a publicly-exposed RDP port.
rules.author: Micah Babinski (@micahbabinski), Zach Mathis (@yamatosecurity)
falsepositives: Legitimate or intentional inbound connections from public IP addresses on the RDP port.

rules.title: External Remote SMB Logon from Public IP
rules.description: Detects successful logon from public IP address via SMB. This can indicate a publicly-exposed SMB port.
rules.author: Micah Babinski (@micahbabinski), Zach Mathis (@yamatosecurity)
falsepositives: Legitimate or intentional inbound connections from public IP addresses on the SMB port.

rules.title: Failed Logon From Public IP
rules.description: Detects a failed logon attempt from a public IP. A login from a public IP can indicate a misconfigured firewall or network boundary.
rules.author: NVISO
falsepositives: Legitimate logon attempts over the internet

rules.title: Outgoing Logon with New Credentials
rules.description: Detects logon events that specify new credentials
rules.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Privilege Escalation via Local Kerberos Relay over LDAP
rules.description:
Detects a suspicious local successful logon event where the Logon Package is Kerberos, the remote address is set to localhost, and the target user SID is the built-in local Administrator account.
This may indicate an attempt to leverage a Kerberos relay attack variant that can be used to elevate privilege locally from a domain joined limited user to local System privileges.
rules.author: Elastic, @SBousseaden

rules.title: RottenPotato Like Attack Pattern
rules.description: Detects logon events that have characteristics of events generated during an attack with RottenPotato and the like
rules.author: @SBousseaden, Florian Roth

rules.title: Successful Account Login Via WMI
rules.description: Detects successful logon attempts performed with WMI
rules.author: Thomas Patzke

rules.title: Windows Filtering Platform Blocked Connection From EDR Agent Binary
rules.description:
Detects a Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) blocked connection event involving common Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents.
Adversaries may use WFP filters to prevent Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents from reporting security events.
rules.author: @gott_cyber

rules.title: Azure AD Health Monitoring Agent Registry Keys Access
rules.description:
This detection uses Windows security events to detect suspicious access attempts to the registry key of Azure AD Health monitoring agent.
This detection requires an access control entry (ACE) on the system access control list (SACL) of the following securable object HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Microsoft Online\Reporting\MonitoringAgent.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

rules.title: Azure AD Health Service Agents Registry Keys Access
rules.description:
This detection uses Windows security events to detect suspicious access attempts to the registry key values and sub-keys of Azure AD Health service agents (e.g AD FS).
Information from AD Health service agents can be used to potentially abuse some of the features provided by those services in the cloud (e.g. Federation).
This detection requires an access control entry (ACE) on the system access control list (SACL) of the following securable object: HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\ADHealthAgent.
Make sure you set the SACL to propagate to its sub-keys.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

rules.title: Powerview Add-DomainObjectAcl DCSync AD Extend Right
rules.description: Backdooring domain object to grant the rights associated with DCSync to a regular user or machine account using Powerview\Add-DomainObjectAcl DCSync Extended Right cmdlet, will allow to re-obtain the pwd hashes of any user/computer
rules.author: Samir Bousseaden, Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, Maxence Fossat

This may indicate an AS-REP Roasting attack, where attackers request AS-REP messages for accounts without pre-authentication and attempt to crack the encrypted ticket offline to recover user passwords.

rules.title: Potential Kerberos Coercion by Spoofing SPNs via DNS Manipulation
rules.description:
Detects modifications to DNS records in Active Directory where the Distinguished Name (DN) contains a base64-encoded blob
matching the pattern "1UWhRCAAAAA...BAAAA". This pattern corresponds to a marshaled CREDENTIAL_TARGET_INFORMATION structure,
commonly used in Kerberos coercion attacks. Adversaries may exploit this to coerce victim systems into authenticating to
attacker-controlled hosts by spoofing SPNs via DNS. It is one of the strong indicators of a Kerberos coercion attack,.
where adversaries manipulate DNS records to spoof Service Principal Names (SPNs) and redirect authentication requests like CVE-2025-33073.
Please investigate the user account that made the changes, as it is likely a low-privileged account that has been compromised.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.description:
Detect suspicious Kerberos TGT requests.
Once an attacer obtains a computer certificate by abusing Active Directory Certificate Services in combination with PetitPotam, the next step would be to leverage the certificate for malicious purposes.
One way of doing this is to request a Kerberos Ticket Granting Ticket using a tool like Rubeus.
This request will generate a 4768 event with some unusual fields depending on the environment.
This analytic will require tuning, we recommend filtering Account_Name to the Domain Controller computer accounts.

rules.title: File Access Of Signal Desktop Sensitive Data
rules.description:
Detects access to Signal Desktop's sensitive data files: db.sqlite and config.json.
The db.sqlite file in Signal Desktop stores all locally saved messages in an encrypted SQLite database, while the config.json contains the decryption key needed to access that data.
Since the key is stored in plain text, a threat actor who gains access to both files can decrypt and read sensitive messages without needing the users credentials.
Currently the rule only covers the default Signal installation path in AppData\Roaming. Signal Portable installations may use different paths based on user configuration. Additional paths can be added to the selection as needed.

falsepositives: Unlikely, but possible from AV or backup software accessing the files.

rules.title: Potential Privileged System Service Operation - SeLoadDriverPrivilege
rules.description:
Detects the usage of the 'SeLoadDriverPrivilege' privilege. This privilege is required to load or unload a device driver.
With this privilege, the user can dynamically load and unload device drivers or other code in to kernel mode.
This user right does not apply to Plug and Play device drivers.
If you exclude privileged users/admins and processes, which are allowed to do so, you are maybe left with bad programs trying to load malicious kernel drivers.
This will detect Ghost-In-The-Logs (https://github.com/bats3c/Ghost-In-The-Logs) and the usage of Sysinternals and various other tools. So you have to work with a whitelist to find the bad stuff.
rules.author: xknow (@xknow_infosec), xorxes (@xor_xes)
falsepositives: Other legimate tools loading drivers. Including but not limited to, Sysinternals, CPU-Z, AVs etc. A baseline needs to be created according to the used products and allowed tools. A good thing to do is to try and exclude users who are allowed to load drivers.

Detects the configuration of a new ISATAP router on a Windows host. While ISATAP is a legitimate Microsoft technology for IPv6 transition, unexpected or unauthorized ISATAP router configurations could indicate a potential IPv6 DNS Takeover attack using tools like mitm6.
In such attacks, adversaries advertise themselves as DHCPv6 servers and set malicious ISATAP routers to intercept traffic.
This detection should be correlated with network baselines and known legitimate ISATAP deployments in your environment.
rules.author: hamid
falsepositives: Legitimate ISATAP router configuration in enterprise environments
IPv6 transition projects and network infrastructure changes
Automatic ISATAP configuration in some Windows deployments

Detects a user certificate that was valid but could not be mapped to a user in a strong way (such as via explicit mapping, key trust mapping, or a SID)
This could be a sign of exploitation of the elevation of privilege vulnerabilities (CVE-2022-34691, CVE-2022-26931, CVE-2022-26923) that can occur when the KDC allows certificate spoofing by not requiring a strong mapping.
Events where the AccountName and CN of the Subject do not match, or where the CN ends in a dollar sign indicating a machine, may indicate certificate spoofing.
rules.author: @br4dy5
falsepositives: If prevalent in the environment, filter on events where the AccountName and CN of the Subject do not reference the same user
If prevalent in the environment, filter on CNs that end in a dollar sign indicating it is a machine name

rules.title: Failed Event Log Clear Via WMI NTEventLogFile ClearEventLog
rules.description:
Detects failed attempts to clear Windows event logs via the WMI NTEventLogFile ClearEventLog method.
Event 5858 in the WMI-Activity operational log is an error event, meaning it is only generated
when the WMI operation encounters an error (e.g. access denied, provider failure).
It could be an indication of an attacker attempting to clear event logs via WMI, but failing due to insufficient privileges or other issues.
Successful clearing operations will NOT produce this event; for those, correlate with
Security event 1102 or System event 104.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Potential CobaltStrike Process Injection

rules.title: Remote Thread Created In KeePass.EXE

rules.title: Remote Thread Creation In Mstsc.Exe From Suspicious Location

Detects remote thread creation in the "mstsc.exe" process by a process located in a potentially suspicious location.
This technique is often used by attackers in order to hook some APIs used by DLLs loaded by "mstsc.exe" during RDP authentications in order to steal credentials.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Credential Dumping Attempt Via PowerShell Remote Thread

rules.title: Remote Thread Creation Via PowerShell In Uncommon Target

rules.title: Password Dumper Remote Thread in LSASS
rules.description:
Detects password dumper activity by monitoring remote thread creation EventID 8 in combination with the lsass.exe process as TargetImage.
The process in field Process is the malicious program. A single execution can lead to hundreds of events.
rules.author: Thomas Patzke

rules.title: Rare Remote Thread Creation By Uncommon Source Image
rules.description: Detects uncommon processes creating remote threads.
rules.author: Perez Diego (@darkquassar), oscd.community
falsepositives: This rule is best put in testing first in order to create a baseline that reflects the data in your environment.

rules.title: Remote Thread Creation By Uncommon Source Image
rules.description: Detects uncommon processes creating remote threads.
rules.author: Perez Diego (@darkquassar), oscd.community
falsepositives: This rule is best put in testing first in order to create a baseline that reflects the data in your environment.

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.description: Detects uncommon target processes for remote thread creation
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Remote Thread Creation Ttdinject.exe Proxy

rules.title: Hidden Executable In NTFS Alternate Data Stream
rules.description: Detects the creation of an ADS (Alternate Data Stream) that contains an executable by looking at a non-empty Imphash
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), @0xrawsec
falsepositives: This rule isn't looking for any particular binary characteristics. As legitimate installers and programs were seen embedding hidden binaries in their ADS. Some false positives are expected from browser processes and similar.

rules.title: Creation Of a Suspicious ADS File Outside a Browser Download
rules.description: Detects the creation of a suspicious ADS (Alternate Data Stream) file by software other than browsers
rules.author: frack113

Legitimate downloads via scripting or command-line tools (Investigate to determine if it's legitimate)

rules.title: Suspicious File Download From File Sharing Websites -  File Stream
rules.description: Detects the download of suspicious file type from a well-known file and paste sharing domain
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Some false positives might occur with binaries download via Github

rules.title: Unusual File Download From File Sharing Websites - File Stream
rules.description: Detects the download of suspicious file type from a well-known file and paste sharing domain
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool Named File Stream Created
rules.description: Detects the creation of a named file stream with the imphash of a well-known hack tool
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Exports Registry Key To an Alternate Data Stream
rules.description: Exports the target Registry key and hides it in the specified alternate data stream.
rules.author: Oddvar Moe, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

rules.title: Unusual File Download from Direct IP Address
rules.description: Detects the download of suspicious file type from URLs with IP
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Suspicious Winget Package Installation
rules.description: Detects potential suspicious winget package installation from a suspicious source.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious File Download From ZIP TLD
rules.description: Detects the download of a file with a potentially suspicious extension from a .zip top level domain.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate file downloads from a websites and web services that uses the ".zip" top level domain.

rules.title: DNS Query for Anonfiles.com Domain - Sysmon
rules.description: Detects DNS queries for "anonfiles.com", which is an anonymous file upload platform often used for malicious purposes
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: AppX Package Installation Attempts Via AppInstaller.EXE
rules.description: Detects DNS queries made by "AppInstaller.EXE". The AppInstaller is the default handler for the "ms-appinstaller" URI. It attempts to load/install a package from the referenced URL
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Cloudflared Tunnels Related DNS Requests
rules.description:
Detects DNS requests to Cloudflared tunnels domains.
Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of cloudflare tunnels will also trigger this.

rules.title: DNS Query To Common Malware Hosting and Shortener Services
rules.description:
Detects DNS queries to domains commonly used by threat actors to host malware payloads or redirect through URL shorteners.
These include platforms like Cloudflare Workers, TryCloudflare, InfinityFree, and URL shorteners such as tinyurl and lihi.cc.
Such DNS activity can indicate potential delivery or command-and-control communication attempts.
rules.author: Ahmed Nosir (@egycondor)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of these services is possible but rare in enterprise environments

rules.title: DNS Query To Devtunnels Domain
rules.description: Detects DNS query requests to Devtunnels domains. Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
rules.author: citron_ninja
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Devtunnels will also trigger this.

rules.title: DNS Server Discovery Via LDAP Query
rules.description: Detects DNS server discovery via LDAP query requests from uncommon applications
rules.author: frack113

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: DNS Query To AzureWebsites.NET By Non-Browser Process
rules.description: Detects a DNS query by a non browser process on the system to "azurewebsites.net". The latter was often used by threat actors as a malware hosting and exfiltration site.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Likely with other browser software. Apply additional filters for any other browsers you might use.

rules.title: DNS Query by Finger Utility
rules.description:
Detects DNS queries made by the finger utility, which can be abused by threat actors to retrieve remote commands for execution on Windows devices.
In one ClickFix malware campaign, adversaries leveraged the finger protocol to fetch commands from a remote server.
Since the finger utility is not commonly used in modern Windows environments, its presence already raises suspicion.
Investigating such DNS queries can also help identify potential malicious infrastructure used by threat actors for command and control (C2) communication.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Notepad++ Updater DNS Query to Uncommon Domains
rules.description:
Detects when the Notepad++ updater (gup.exe) makes DNS queries to domains that are not part of the known legitimate update infrastructure.
This could indicate potential exploitation of the updater mechanism or suspicious network activity that warrants further investigation.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Some legitimate network misconfigurations or proxy issues causing unexpected DNS queries.
Other legitimate query to official domains not listed in the filter, needing tuning.

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: DNS HybridConnectionManager Service Bus
rules.description: Detects Azure Hybrid Connection Manager services querying the Azure service bus service
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Azure Hybrid Connection Manager and the Azure Service Bus service

rules.title: Suspicious DNS Query Indicating Kerberos Coercion via DNS Object SPN Spoofing
rules.description:
Detects DNS queries containing patterns associated with Kerberos coercion attacks via DNS object spoofing.
The pattern "1UWhRCAAAAA..BAAAA" is a base64-encoded signature that corresponds to a marshaled CREDENTIAL_TARGET_INFORMATION structure.
Attackers can use this technique to coerce authentication from victim systems to attacker-controlled hosts.
It is one of the strong indicators of a Kerberos coercion attack, where adversaries manipulate DNS records
to spoof Service Principal Names (SPNs) and redirect authentication requests like CVE-2025-33073.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Cobalt Strike DNS Beaconing - Sysmon
rules.description: Detects a program that invoked suspicious DNS queries known from Cobalt Strike beacons
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DNS Query To MEGA Hosting Website
rules.description: Detects DNS queries for subdomains related to MEGA sharing website
rules.author: Aaron Greetham (@beardofbinary) - NCC Group
falsepositives: Legitimate DNS queries and usage of Mega

rules.title: DNS Query Request To OneLaunch Update Service
rules.description:
Detects DNS query requests to "update.onelaunch.com". This domain is associated with the OneLaunch adware application.
When the OneLaunch application is installed it will attempt to get updates from this domain.
rules.author: Josh Nickels

rules.title: DNS Query Request By QuickAssist.EXE
rules.description: Detects DNS queries initiated by "QuickAssist.exe" to Microsoft Quick Assist primary endpoint that is used to establish a session.
rules.author: Muhammad Faisal (@faisalusuf)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Quick Assist in the environment.

rules.title: DNS Query Request By Regsvr32.EXE
rules.description: Detects DNS queries initiated by "Regsvr32.exe"
rules.author: Dmitriy Lifanov, oscd.community

rules.title: DNS Query To Remote Access Software Domain From Non-Browser App
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)
rules.author: frack113, Connor Martin
falsepositives: Likely with other browser software. Apply additional filters for any other browsers you might use.

detection.condition: 1 of selection_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Suspicious DNS Query for IP Lookup Service APIs
rules.description: Detects DNS queries for IP lookup services such as "api.ipify.org" originating from a non browser process.
rules.author: Brandon George (blog post), Thomas Patzke
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of IP lookup services such as ipify API

rules.title: TeamViewer Domain Query By Non-TeamViewer Application
rules.description: Detects DNS queries to a TeamViewer domain only resolved by a TeamViewer client by an image that isn't named TeamViewer (sometimes used by threat actors for obfuscation)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Depending on the environment the rule might require some initial tuning before usage to avoid FP with third party applications

rules.title: DNS Query Tor .Onion Address - Sysmon
rules.description: Detects DNS queries to an ".onion" address related to Tor routing networks
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: DNS Query To Ufile.io
rules.description: Detects DNS queries to "ufile.io", which was seen abused by malware and threat actors as a method for data exfiltration
rules.author: yatinwad, TheDFIRReport
falsepositives: DNS queries for "ufile" are not malicious by nature necessarily. Investigate the source to determine the necessary actions to take

rules.title: DNS Query To Visual Studio Code Tunnels Domain
rules.description: Detects DNS query requests to Visual Studio Code tunnel domains. Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
rules.author: citron_ninja
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Visual Studio Code tunnel will also trigger this.

rules.title: Malicious Driver Load By Name
rules.description: Detects loading of known malicious drivers via the file name of the drivers.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: False positives may occur if one of the vulnerable driver names mentioned above didn't change its name between versions. So always make sure that the driver being loaded is the legitimate one and the non vulnerable version.
If you experience a lot of FP you could comment the driver name or its exact known legitimate location (when possible)

rules.title: Malicious Driver Load
rules.description: Detects loading of known malicious drivers via their hash.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - Process Hacker Driver Load
rules.description: Detects driver load of the Process Hacker tool
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of process hacker or system informer by developers or system administrators

rules.title: PUA - System Informer Driver Load
rules.description: Detects driver load of the System Informer tool
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: System Informer is regularly used legitimately by system administrators or developers. Apply additional filters accordingly

rules.title: Driver Load From A Temporary Directory
rules.description: Detects a driver load from a temporary directory
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: There is a relevant set of false positives depending on applications in the environment

rules.title: Vulnerable Driver Load By Name
rules.description: Detects the load of known vulnerable drivers via the file name of the drivers.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: False positives may occur if one of the vulnerable driver names mentioned above didn't change its name between versions. So always make sure that the driver being loaded is the legitimate one and the non vulnerable version.
If you experience a lot of FP you could comment the driver name or its exact known legitimate location (when possible)

rules.title: Vulnerable Driver Load
rules.description: Detects loading of known vulnerable drivers via their hash.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Vulnerable HackSys Extreme Vulnerable Driver Load
rules.description: Detects the load of HackSys Extreme Vulnerable Driver which is an intentionally vulnerable Windows driver developed for security enthusiasts to learn and polish their exploitation skills at Kernel level and often abused by threat actors
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Vulnerable WinRing0 Driver Load
rules.description: Detects the load of a signed WinRing0 driver often used by threat actors, crypto miners (XMRIG) or malware for privilege escalation
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: WinDivert Driver Load
rules.description: Detects the load of the Windiver driver, a powerful user-mode capture/sniffing/modification/blocking/re-injection package for Windows
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Unusual File Modification by dns.exe
rules.description: Detects an unexpected file being modified by dns.exe which my indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)
rules.author: Tim Rauch (Nextron Systems), Elastic (idea)

rules.title: Backup Files Deleted
rules.description: Detects deletion of files with extensions often used for backup files. Adversaries may delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off services designed to aid in the recovery of a corrupted system to prevent recovery.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: EventLog EVTX File Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the event log files which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Exchange PowerShell Cmdlet History Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the Exchange PowerShell cmdlet History logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: IIS WebServer Access Logs Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of IIS WebServer access logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Tim Rauch (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: During uninstallation of the IIS service

rules.title: Process Deletion of Its Own Executable
rules.description: Detects the deletion of a process's executable by itself. This is usually not possible without workarounds and may be used by malware to hide its traces.
rules.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Some false positives are to be expected from uninstallers.

rules.title: PowerShell Console History Logs Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the PowerShell console History logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Prefetch File Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of a prefetch file which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Cedric MAURUGEON

rules.title: TeamViewer Log File Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the TeamViewer log files which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Tomcat WebServer Logs Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of tomcat WebServer logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: During uninstallation of the tomcat server

rules.title: File Deleted Via Sysinternals SDelete
rules.description: Detects the deletion of files by the Sysinternals SDelete utility. It looks for the common name pattern used to rename files.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

rules.title: Unusual File Deletion by Dns.exe
rules.description: Detects an unexpected file being deleted by dns.exe which my indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)
rules.author: Tim Rauch (Nextron Systems), Elastic (idea)

rules.title: ADS Zone.Identifier Deleted By Uncommon Application
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the "Zone.Identifier" ADS by an uncommon process. Attackers can leverage this in order to bypass security restrictions that make use of the ADS such as Microsoft Office apps.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Other third party applications not listed.

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: ADSI-Cache File Creation By Uncommon Tool
rules.description: Detects the creation of an "Active Directory Schema Cache File" (.sch) file by an uncommon tool.
rules.author: xknow @xknow_infosec, Tim Shelton
falsepositives: Other legimate tools, which do ADSI (LDAP) operations, e.g. any remoting activity by MMC, Powershell, Windows etc.

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Advanced IP Scanner - File Event
rules.description: Detects the use of Advanced IP Scanner. Seems to be a popular tool for ransomware groups.
rules.author: @ROxPinTeddy

rules.title: Anydesk Temporary Artefact
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Suspicious Binary Writes Via AnyDesk
rules.description:
Detects AnyDesk writing binary files to disk other than "gcapi.dll".
According to RedCanary research it is highly abnormal for AnyDesk to write executable files to disk besides gcapi.dll,
which is a legitimate DLL that is part of the Google Chrome web browser used to interact with the Google Cloud API. (See reference section for more details)
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious File Created by ArcSOC.exe
rules.description:
Detects instances where the ArcGIS Server process ArcSOC.exe, which hosts REST services running on an ArcGIS
server, creates a file with suspicious file type, indicating that it may be an executable, script file,
or otherwise unusual.
rules.author: Micah Babinski

rules.title: Assembly DLL Creation Via AspNetCompiler
rules.description: Detects the creation of new DLL assembly files by "aspnet_compiler.exe", which could be a sign of "aspnet_compiler" abuse to proxy execution through a build provider.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate assembly compilation using a build provider

rules.title: BloodHound Collection Files
rules.description: Detects default file names outputted by the BloodHound collection tool SharpHound
rules.author: C.J. May
falsepositives: Some false positives may arise in some environment and this may require some tuning. Add additional filters or reduce level depending on the level of noise

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious File Creation by OpenEDR's ITSMService
rules.description:
Detects the creation of potentially suspicious files by OpenEDR's ITSMService process.
The ITSMService is responsible for remote management operations and can create files on the system through the Process Explorer or file management features.
While legitimate for IT operations, creation of executable or script files could indicate unauthorized file uploads, data staging, or malicious file deployment.
rules.author: @kostastsale
falsepositives: Authorized remote file uploads by IT administrators

rules.title: EVTX Created In Uncommon Location
rules.description:
Detects the creation of new files with the ".evtx" extension in non-common or non-standard location.
This could indicate tampering with default EVTX locations in order to evade security controls or simply exfiltration of event log to search for sensitive information within.
Note that backup software and legitimate administrator might perform similar actions during troubleshooting.
rules.author: D3F7A5105
falsepositives: An unknown bug seems to trigger the Windows "svchost" process to drop EVTX files in the "C:\Windows\Temp" directory in the form "<log_name">_<uuid>.evtx". See https://superuser.com/questions/1371229/low-disk-space-after-filling-up-c-windows-temp-with-evtx-and-txt-files

rules.title: Creation Of Non-Existent System DLL
rules.description:
Detects creation of specific system DLL files that are  usually not present on the system (or at least not in system directories) but may be loaded by legitimate processes.
Phantom DLL hijacking involves placing malicious DLLs with names of non-existent system binaries in locations where legitimate applications may search for them, leading to execution of the malicious DLLs.
Thus, the creation of such DLLs may indicate preparation for phantom DLL hijacking attacks.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), fornotes

rules.title: Suspicious Deno File Written from Remote Source
rules.description:
Detects Deno writing a file from a direct HTTP(s) call and writing to the appdata folder or bringing it's own malicious DLL.
This behavior may indicate an attempt to execute remotely hosted, potentially malicious files through deno.
rules.author: Josh Nickels, Michael Taggart
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of deno to request a file or bring a DLL to a host

rules.title: New Custom Shim Database Created
rules.description:
Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims.
The Microsoft Windows Application Compatibility Infrastructure/Framework (Application Shim) was created to allow for backward compatibility of software as the operating system codebase changes over time.
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate custom SHIM installations will also trigger this rule

rules.title: Suspicious Screensaver Binary File Creation
rules.description:
Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by user inactivity.
Screensavers are programs that execute after a configurable time of user inactivity and consist of Portable Executable (PE) files with a .scr file extension
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Files With System DLL Name In Unsuspected Locations
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a file with the ".dll" extension that has the name of a System DLL in uncommon or unsuspected locations. (Outisde of "System32", "SysWOW64", etc.).
It is highly recommended to perform an initial baseline before using this rule in production.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Third party software might bundle specific versions of system DLLs.

rules.title: Files With System Process Name In Unsuspected Locations
rules.description:
Detects the creation of an executable with a system process name in folders other than the system ones (System32, SysWOW64, etc.).
It is highly recommended to perform an initial baseline before using this rule in production.
rules.author: Sander Wiebing, Tim Shelton, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: System processes copied outside their default folders for testing purposes
Third party software naming their software with the same names as the processes mentioned here

rules.title: Creation Exe for Service with Unquoted Path
rules.description:
Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking vulnerable file path references.
Adversaries can take advantage of paths that lack surrounding quotations by placing an executable in a higher level directory within the path, so that Windows will choose the adversary's executable to launch.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Cred Dump Tools Dropped Files
rules.description: Files with well-known filenames (parts of credential dump software or files produced by them) creation
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community
falsepositives: Legitimate Administrator using tool for password recovery

rules.title: WScript or CScript Dropper - File
rules.description: Detects a file ending in jse, vbe, js, vba, vbs, wsf, wsh written by cscript.exe or wscript.exe
rules.author: Tim Shelton

rules.title: CSExec Service File Creation
rules.description: Detects default CSExec service filename which indicates CSExec service installation and execution
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Dynamic CSharp Compile Artefact
rules.description:
When C# is compiled dynamically, a .cmdline file will be created as a part of the process.
Certain processes are not typically observed compiling C# code, but can do so without touching disk.
This can be used to unpack a payload for execution
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Potential DCOM InternetExplorer.Application DLL Hijack
rules.description: Detects potential DLL hijack of "iertutil.dll" found in the DCOM InternetExplorer.Application Class over the network
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR), wagga

rules.title: Desktop.INI Created by Uncommon Process
rules.description: Detects unusual processes accessing desktop.ini, which can be leveraged to alter how Explorer displays a folder's content (i.e. renaming files) without changing them on disk.
rules.author: Maxime Thiebaut (@0xThiebaut), Tim Shelton (HAWK.IO)
falsepositives: Operations performed through Windows SCCM or equivalent

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: DLL Search Order Hijackig Via Additional Space in Path
rules.description:
Detects when an attacker create a similar folder structure to windows system folders such as (Windows, Program Files...)
but with a space in order to trick DLL load search order and perform a "DLL Search Order Hijacking" attack
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious DMP/HDMP File Creation
rules.description: Detects the creation of a file with the ".dmp"/".hdmp" extension by a shell or scripting application such as "cmd", "powershell", etc. Often created by software during a crash. Memory dumps can sometimes contain sensitive information such as credentials. It's best to determine the source of the crash.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Some administrative PowerShell or VB scripts might have the ability to collect dumps and move them to other folders which might trigger a false positive.

rules.title: Potential Persistence Attempt Via ErrorHandler.Cmd
rules.description:
Detects creation of a file named "ErrorHandler.cmd" in the "C:\WINDOWS\Setup\Scripts\" directory which could be used as a method of persistence
The content of C:\WINDOWS\Setup\Scripts\ErrorHandler.cmd is read whenever some tools under C:\WINDOWS\System32\oobe\ (e.g. Setup.exe) fail to run for any reason.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious File Drop by Exchange
rules.description: Detects suspicious file type dropped by an Exchange component in IIS
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious ASPX File Drop by Exchange
rules.description: Detects suspicious file type dropped by an Exchange component in IIS into a suspicious folder
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), MSTI (query, idea)

rules.title: GoToAssist Temporary Installation Artefact
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Uncommon File Created by Notepad++ Updater Gup.EXE
rules.description:
Detects when the Notepad++ updater (gup.exe) creates files in suspicious or uncommon locations.
This could indicate potential exploitation of the updater component to deliver unwanted malware or unwarranted files.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Custom or portable Notepad++ installations in non-standard directories.
Legitimate update processes creating temporary files in unexpected locations.

rules.title: HackTool - CrackMapExec File Indicators
rules.description: Detects file creation events with filename patterns used by CrackMapExec.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Dumpert Process Dumper Default File
rules.description: Detects the creation of the default dump file used by Outflank Dumpert tool. A process dumper, which dumps the lsass process memory
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Typical HiveNightmare SAM File Export
rules.description: Detects files written by the different tools that exploit HiveNightmare
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Files that accidentally contain these strings

rules.title: HackTool - Inveigh Execution Artefacts
rules.description: Detects the presence and execution of Inveigh via dropped artefacts
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - RemoteKrbRelay SMB Relay Secrets Dump Module Indicators
rules.description: Detects the creation of file with specific names used by RemoteKrbRelay SMB Relay attack module.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Mimikatz Kirbi File Creation
rules.description: Detects the creation of files created by mimikatz such as ".kirbi", "mimilsa.log", etc.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), David ANDRE

rules.title: HackTool - NetExec File Indicators
rules.description:
Detects file creation events indicating NetExec (nxc.exe) execution on the local machine.
NetExec is a PyInstaller-bundled binary that extracts its embedded data files to a "_MEI<random>" directory
under the Temp folder upon execution. Files dropped under the "\nxc\" sub-directory of that
extraction path are unique to NetExec and serve as reliable on-disk indicators of execution.
NetExec (formerly CrackMapExec) is a widely used post-exploitation and lateral movement tool used for
Active Directory enumeration, credential harvesting, and remote code execution.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - NPPSpy Hacktool Usage
rules.description: Detects the use of NPPSpy hacktool that stores cleartext passwords of users that logged in to a local file
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Powerup Write Hijack DLL
rules.description:
Powerup tool's Write Hijack DLL exploits DLL hijacking for privilege escalation.
In it's default mode, it builds a self deleting .bat file which executes malicious command.
The detection rule relies on creation of the malicious bat file (debug.bat by default).
rules.author: Subhash Popuri (@pbssubhash)
falsepositives: Any powershell script that creates bat files

rules.title: HackTool - QuarksPwDump Dump File
rules.description: Detects a dump file written by QuarksPwDump password dumper
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Potential Remote Credential Dumping Activity Via CrackMapExec Or Impacket-Secretsdump
rules.description: Detects default filenames output from the execution of CrackMapExec and Impacket-secretsdump against an endpoint.
rules.author: SecurityAura

rules.title: HackTool - SafetyKatz Dump Indicator
rules.description: Detects default lsass dump filename generated by SafetyKatz.
rules.author: Markus Neis
falsepositives: Rare legitimate files with similar filename structure

rules.title: HackTool - Impacket File Indicators
rules.description: Detects file creation events with filename patterns used by Impacket.
rules.author: The DFIR Report, IrishDeath

rules.title: Potential Initial Access via DLL Search Order Hijacking
rules.description: Detects attempts to create a DLL file to a known desktop application dependencies folder such as Slack, Teams or OneDrive and by an unusual process. This may indicate an attempt to load a malicious module via DLL search order hijacking.
rules.author: Tim Rauch (rule), Elastic (idea)

rules.title: Installation of TeamViewer Desktop
rules.description: TeamViewer_Desktop.exe is create during install
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Malicious DLL File Dropped in the Teams or OneDrive Folder
rules.description:
Detects creation of a malicious DLL file in the location where the OneDrive or Team applications
Upon execution of the Teams or OneDrive application, the dropped malicious DLL file ("iphlpapi.dll") is sideloaded
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: ISO File Created Within Temp Folders
rules.description: Detects the creation of a ISO file in the Outlook temp folder or in the Appdata temp folder. Typical of Qakbot TTP from end-July 2022.
rules.author: @sam0x90
falsepositives: Potential FP by sysadmin opening a zip file containing a legitimate ISO file

rules.title: ISO or Image Mount Indicator in Recent Files
rules.description:
Detects the creation of recent element file that points to an .ISO, .IMG, .VHD or .VHDX file as often used in phishing attacks.
This can be a false positive on server systems but on workstations users should rarely mount .iso or .img files.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Cases in which a user mounts an image file for legitimate reasons

rules.title: GatherNetworkInfo.VBS Reconnaissance Script Output
rules.description: Detects creation of files which are the results of executing the built-in reconnaissance script "C:\Windows\System32\gatherNetworkInfo.vbs".
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: LSASS Process Memory Dump Files
rules.description: Detects creation of files with names used by different memory dumping tools to create a memory dump of the LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: LSASS Process Dump Artefact In CrashDumps Folder
rules.description: Detects the presence of an LSASS dump file in the "CrashDumps" folder. This could be a sign of LSASS credential dumping. Techniques such as the LSASS Shtinkering have been seen abusing the Windows Error Reporting to dump said process.
rules.author: @pbssubhash
falsepositives: Rare legitimate dump of the process by the operating system due to a crash of lsass

rules.title: WerFault LSASS Process Memory Dump
rules.description: Detects WerFault creating a dump file with a name that indicates that the dump file could be an LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Adwind RAT / JRAT File Artifact
rules.description: Detects javaw.exe in AppData folder as used by Adwind / JRAT
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tom Ueltschi, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Octopus Scanner Malware
rules.description: Detects Octopus Scanner Malware.
rules.author: NVISO

rules.title: File Creation In Suspicious Directory By Msdt.EXE
rules.description: Detects msdt.exe creating files in suspicious directories which could be a sign of exploitation of either Follina or Dogwalk vulnerabilities
rules.author: Vadim Varganov, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon File Creation By Mysql Daemon Process
rules.description:
Detects the creation of files with scripting or executable extensions by Mysql daemon.
Which could be an indicator of "User Defined Functions" abuse to download malware.
rules.author: Joseph Kamau

rules.title: Suspicious DotNET CLR Usage Log Artifact
rules.description: Detects the creation of Usage Log files by the CLR (clr.dll). These files are named after the executing process once the assembly is finished executing for the first time in the (user) session context.
rules.author: frack113, omkar72, oscd.community, Wojciech Lesicki
falsepositives: Rundll32.exe with zzzzInvokeManagedCustomActionOutOfProc in command line and msiexec.exe as parent process - https://twitter.com/SBousseaden/status/1388064061087260675

rules.title: Suspicious File Creation In Uncommon AppData Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of suspicious files and folders inside the user's AppData folder but not inside any of the common and well known directories (Local, Romaing, LocalLow). This method could be used as a method to bypass detection who exclude the AppData folder in fear of FPs
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: SCR File Write Event
rules.description: Detects the creation of screensaver files (.scr) outside of system folders. Attackers may execute an application as an ".SCR" file using "rundll32.exe desk.cpl,InstallScreenSaver" for example.
rules.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io
falsepositives: The installation of new screen savers by third party software

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Notepad++ Plugins
rules.description: Detects creation of new ".dll" files inside the plugins directory of a notepad++ installation by a process other than "gup.exe". Which could indicates possible persistence
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Possible FPs during first installation of Notepad++
Legitimate use of custom plugins by users in order to enhance notepad++ functionalities

rules.title: NTDS.DIT Created
rules.description: Detects creation of a file named "ntds.dit" (Active Directory Database)
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: NTDS.DIT Creation By Uncommon Parent Process
rules.description: Detects creation of a file named "ntds.dit" (Active Directory Database) by an uncommon parent process or directory
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: NTDS.DIT Creation By Uncommon Process
