Detects a command line process that uses explorer.exe to launch arbitrary commands or binaries,
which is similar to cmd.exe /c, only it breaks the process tree and makes its parent a new instance of explorer spawning from "svchost"
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), @gott_cyber

rules.title: File Explorer Folder Opened Using Explorer Folder Shortcut Via Shell
rules.description: Detects the initial execution of "cmd.exe" which spawns "explorer.exe" with the appropriate command line arguments for opening the "My Computer" folder.
rules.author: @Kostastsale

rules.title: Explorer NOUACCHECK Flag
rules.description: Detects suspicious starts of explorer.exe that use the /NOUACCHECK flag that allows to run all sub processes of that newly started explorer.exe without any UAC checks
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Unknown how many legitimate software products use that method

rules.title: Remote File Download Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "findstr" with specific flags and a remote share path. This specific set of CLI flags would allow "findstr" to download the content of the file located on the remote share as described in the LOLBAS entry.
rules.author: Furkan CALISKAN, @caliskanfurkan_, @oscd_initiative, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Findstr GPP Passwords
rules.description: Look for the encrypted cpassword value within Group Policy Preference files on the Domain Controller. This value can be decrypted with gpp-decrypt.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Findstr Launching .lnk File
rules.description: Detects usage of findstr to identify and execute a lnk file as seen within the HHS redirect attack
rules.author: Trent Liffick

rules.title: LSASS Process Reconnaissance Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects findstring commands that include the keyword lsass, which indicates recon actviity for the LSASS process PID
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Permission Misconfiguration Reconnaissance Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description:
Detects usage of findstr with the "EVERYONE" or "BUILTIN" keywords.
This was seen being used in combination with "icacls" and other utilities to spot misconfigured files or folders permissions.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Recon Command Output Piped To Findstr.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of a potential recon command where the results are piped to "findstr". This is meant to trigger on inline calls of "cmd.exe" via the "/c" or "/k" for example.
Attackers often time use this technique to extract specific information they require in their reconnaissance phase.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), frack113

rules.title: Security Tools Keyword Lookup Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of "findstr" to search for common names of security tools. Attackers often pipe the results of recon commands such as "tasklist" or "whoami" to "findstr" in order to filter out the results.
This detection focuses on the keywords that the attacker might use as a filter.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), frack113

rules.title: Insensitive Subfolder Search Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of findstr with the "s" and "i" flags for a "subfolder" and "insensitive" search respectively. Attackers sometimes leverage this built-in utility to search the system for interesting files or filter through results of commands.
rules.author: Furkan CALISKAN, @caliskanfurkan_, @oscd_initiative, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Sysmon Discovery Via Default Driver Altitude Using Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of "findstr" with the argument "385201". Which could indicate potential discovery of an installed Sysinternals Sysmon service using the default driver altitude (even if the name is changed).
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Finger.EXE Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of the "finger.exe" utility.
Finger.EXE or "TCPIP Finger Command" is an old utility that is still present on modern Windows installation. It Displays information about users on a specified remote computer (typically a UNIX computer) that is running the finger service or daemon.
Due to the old nature of this utility and the rareness of machines having the finger service. Any execution of "finger.exe" can be considered "suspicious" and worth investigating.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), omkar72, oscd.community
falsepositives: Admin activity (unclear what they do nowadays with finger.exe)

rules.title: Sysmon Driver Unloaded Via Fltmc.EXE
rules.description: Detects possible Sysmon filter driver unloaded via fltmc.exe
rules.author: Kirill Kiryanov, oscd.community

rules.title: Filter Driver Unloaded Via Fltmc.EXE
rules.description: Detect filter driver unloading activity via fltmc.exe
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Forfiles.EXE Child Process Masquerading
rules.description: Detects the execution of "forfiles" from a non-default location, in order to potentially spawn a custom "cmd.exe" from the current working directory.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Anish Bogati

rules.title: Forfiles Command Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "forfiles" with the "/c" flag.
While this is an expected behavior of the tool, it can be abused in order to proxy execution through it with any binary.
Can be used to bypass application whitelisting.
rules.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic, E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community
falsepositives: Legitimate use via a batch script or by an administrator.

rules.title: Uncommon FileSystem Load Attempt By Format.com
rules.description: Detects the execution of format.com with an uncommon filesystem selection that could indicate a defense evasion activity in which "format.com" is used to load malicious DLL files or other programs.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Use of FSharp Interpreters
rules.description:
Detects the execution of FSharp Interpreters "FsiAnyCpu.exe" and "FSi.exe"
Both can be used for AWL bypass and to execute F# code via scripts or inline.
rules.author: Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io
falsepositives: Legitimate use by a software developer.

rules.title: Fsutil Drive Enumeration
rules.description: Attackers may leverage fsutil to enumerated connected drives.
rules.author: Christopher Peacock '@securepeacock', SCYTHE '@scythe_io'
references: Turla has used fsutil fsinfo drives to list connected drives.
falsepositives: Certain software or administrative tasks may trigger false positives.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious NTFS Symlink Behavior Modification
rules.description: Detects the modification of NTFS symbolic link behavior using fsutil, which could be used to enable remote to local or remote to remote symlinks for potential attacks.
rules.author: frack113, The DFIR Report
falsepositives: Legitimate usage, investigate the parent process and context to determine if benign.

rules.title: Fsutil Suspicious Invocation
rules.description:
Detects suspicious parameters of fsutil (deleting USN journal, configuring it with small size, etc).
Might be used by ransomwares during the attack (seen by NotPetya and others).
rules.author: Ecco, E.M. Anhaus, oscd.community
falsepositives: Scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: Potential Arbitrary Command Execution Via FTP.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "ftp.exe" script with the "-s" or "/s" flag and any child processes ran by "ftp.exe".
rules.author: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community

rules.title: Arbitrary File Download Via GfxDownloadWrapper.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of GfxDownloadWrapper.exe with a URL as an argument to download file.
rules.author: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community

rules.title: Suspicious Git Clone
rules.description: Detects execution of "git" in order to clone a remote repository that contain suspicious keywords which might be suspicious
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Github Self-Hosted Runner Execution
rules.description:
Detects GitHub self-hosted runners executing workflows on local infrastructure that could be abused for persistence and code execution.
Shai-Hulud is an npm supply chain worm targeting CI/CD environments.
It installs runners on compromised systems to maintain access after credential theft, leveraging their access to secrets and internal networks.
rules.author: Daniel Koifman (KoifSec)
falsepositives: Legitimate GitHub self-hosted runner installations on designated CI/CD infrastructure
Authorized runner deployments by DevOps/Platform teams following change management
Scheduled runner updates or reconfigurations on existing build agents
Self-hosted runners that follow expected/known naming patterns
Installation via expected/known configuration management tools (reflected mostly as parent process name)

detection.condition: all of selection_worker_* or all of selection_listener_*

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious GoogleUpdate Child Process
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of "GoogleUpdate.exe"
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: File Decryption Using Gpg4win
rules.description: Detects usage of Gpg4win to decrypt files
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: File Encryption Using Gpg4win
rules.description: Detects usage of Gpg4win to encrypt files
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Portable Gpg.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of "gpg.exe" from uncommon location. Often used by ransomware and loaders to decrypt/encrypt data.
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: File Encryption/Decryption Via Gpg4win From Suspicious Locations
rules.description: Detects usage of Gpg4win to encrypt/decrypt files located in potentially suspicious locations.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Gpresult Display Group Policy Information
rules.description: Detects cases in which a user uses the built-in Windows utility gpresult to display the Resultant Set of Policy (RSoP) information
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Arbitrary Binary Execution Using GUP Utility
rules.description: Detects execution of the Notepad++ updater (gup) to launch other commands or executables
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Other parent binaries using GUP not currently identified

rules.title: File Download Using Notepad++ GUP Utility
rules.description: Detects execution of the Notepad++ updater (gup) from a process other than Notepad++ to download files.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Other parent processes other than notepad++ using GUP that are not currently identified

Threat actors and red teams commonly use NetExec to identify vulnerable systems, harvest credentials, and execute commands remotely.

rules.title: Attempts of Kerberos Coercion Via DNS SPN Spoofing
rules.description:
Detects the presence of "UWhRC....AAYBAAAA" pattern in command line.
The pattern "1UWhRCAAAAA..BAAAA" is a base64-encoded signature that corresponds to a marshaled CREDENTIAL_TARGET_INFORMATION structure.
Attackers can use this technique to coerce authentication from victim systems to attacker-controlled hosts.
It is one of the strong indicators of a Kerberos coercion attack, where adversaries manipulate DNS records
to spoof Service Principal Names (SPNs) and redirect authentication requests like in CVE-2025-33073.
If you see this pattern in the command line, it is likely an attempt to add spoofed Service Principal Names (SPNs) to DNS records,
or checking for the presence of such records through the `nslookup` command.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon Link.EXE Parent Process
rules.description:
Detects an uncommon parent process of "LINK.EXE".
Link.EXE in Microsoft incremental linker. Its a utility usually bundled with Visual Studio installation.
Multiple utilities often found in the same folder (editbin.exe, dumpbin.exe, lib.exe, etc) have a hardcode call to the "LINK.EXE" binary without checking its validity.
This would allow an attacker to sideload any binary with the name "link.exe" if one of the aforementioned tools get executed from a different location.
By filtering the known locations of such utilities we can spot uncommon parent process of LINK.EXE that might be suspicious or malicious.

rules.title: New Agent Skills Installation Attempt Via Node.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the attempt to install new skills for AI agents using the "npx skills" command.
Agent skills enhance AI agents with new capabilities, but attackers may abuse this mechanism to inject malicious commands executed by the agent on behalf of the user.
The "npx skills" command can install skills for various agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, and others).
Analysts should review any installed skills to verify their legitimacy.
Note: Tune this rule based on whether AI agent tooling is allowed in your environment.
In environments where such tooling is authorized, this detection may reflect normal activity and the alert level should be adjusted accordingly.
In environments where AI agent tooling is not permitted, this activity is likely suspicious and may require immediate investigation.
rules.author: Marco Pedrinazzi (@pedrinazziM) (InTheCyber)
falsepositives: This rule will be triggered when a new agent skill is installed regardless if it is benign or malicious.
High false positive rate expected in environments where AI agent tooling is authorized and commonly used.

Detects the execution of PowerShell commands that attempt to install MSI packages via the
Windows Installer COM object (`WindowsInstaller.Installer`) hosted remotely.
This could be indication of malicious software deployment or lateral movement attempts using Windows Installer functionality.
And the usage of WindowsInstaller COM object rather than msiexec could be an attempt to bypass the detection.

rules.title: Obfuscated PowerShell MSI Install via WindowsInstaller COM
rules.description:
Detects the execution of obfuscated PowerShell commands that attempt to install MSI packages via the Windows Installer COM object (`WindowsInstaller.Installer`).
The technique involves manipulating strings to hide functionality, such as constructing class names using string insertion (e.g., 'indowsInstaller.Installer'.Insert(0,'W')) and correcting
malformed URLs (e.g., converting 'htps://' to 'https://') at runtime. This behavior is commonly associated with malware loaders or droppers that aim to bypass static detection
by hiding intent in runtime-generated strings and using legitimate tools for code execution. The use of `InstallProduct` and COM object creation, particularly combined with
hidden window execution and suppressed UI, indicates an attempt to install software (likely malicious) without user interaction.
rules.author: Meroujan Antonyan (vx3r)

The DSInternals PowerShell Module exposes several internal features of Active Directory and Azure Active Directory. These include FIDO2 and NGC key auditing, offline ntds.dit file manipulation, password auditing, DC recovery from IFM backups and password hash calculation.

rules.title: PUA - Fast Reverse Proxy (FRP) Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of Fast Reverse Proxy. frp is a fast reverse proxy to help you expose a local server behind a NAT or firewall to the Internet.
rules.author: frack113, Florian Roth

rules.title: PUA- IOX Tunneling Tool Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of IOX - a tool for port forwarding and intranet proxy purposes
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - Kernel Driver Utility (KDU) Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of the Kernel Driver Utility (KDU) tool.
KDU can be used to bypass driver signature enforcement and load unsigned or malicious drivers into the Windows kernel.
Potentially allowing for privilege escalation, persistence, or evasion of security controls.
rules.author: Matt Anderson, Dray Agha, Anna Pham (Huntress)
falsepositives: Legitimate driver development, testing, or administrative troubleshooting (e.g., enabling/disabling hardware)

rules.title: PUA - Memory Dump Mount Via MemProcFS
rules.description:
Detects execution of MemProcFS a memory forensics tool with the '-device' parameter.
MemProcFS mounts physical memory as a virtual file system, allowing direct access to process memory and system structures.
Threat actors were seen abusing this utility to mount memory dumps and then extract sensitive information from processes like LSASS or extract registry hives to obtain credentials, LSA secrets, SAM data, and cached domain credentials.
MemProcFS usage that is not part of authorized forensic analysis should be treated as suspicious and warrants further investigation.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use during memory forensics; if not part of authorized analysis, warrants urgent investigation

rules.title: PUA - Mouse Lock Execution
rules.description: In Kaspersky's 2020 Incident Response Analyst Report they listed legitimate tool "Mouse Lock" as being used for both credential access and collection in security incidents.
rules.author: Cian Heasley
falsepositives: Legitimate uses of Mouse Lock software

rules.title: PUA - Netcat Suspicious Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of Netcat. Adversaries may use a non-application layer protocol for communication between host and C2 server or among infected hosts within a network
rules.author: frack113, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - SoftPerfect Netscan Execution
rules.description:
Detects usage of SoftPerfect's "netscan.exe". An application for scanning networks.
It is actively used in-the-wild by threat actors to inspect and understand the network architecture of a victim.
rules.author: @d4ns4n_ (Wuerth-Phoenix)

rules.title: PUA - Ngrok Execution
rules.description:
Detects the use of Ngrok, a utility used for port forwarding and tunneling, often used by threat actors to make local protected services publicly available.
Involved domains are bin.equinox.io for download and *.ngrok.io for connections.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Another tool that uses the command line switches of Ngrok

rules.title: PUA - Nimgrab Execution
rules.description: Detects the usage of nimgrab, a tool bundled with the Nim programming framework and used for downloading files.
rules.author: frack113
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Nim on a developer systems

rules.title: PUA - NimScan Execution
rules.description:
Detects usage of NimScan, a portscanner utility.
In early 2025, adversaries were observed using this utility to scan for open ports on remote hosts in a compromised environment.
This rule identifies the execution of NimScan based on the process image name and specific hash values associated with different versions of the tool.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - NirCmd Execution As LOCAL SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects the use of NirCmd tool for command execution as SYSTEM user
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - NirCmd Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of NirCmd tool for command execution, which could be the result of legitimate administrative activity
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: 1 of selection_* or all of combo_*

rules.title: PUA - Nmap/Zenmap Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of namp/zenmap. Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including those that may be vulnerable to remote software exploitation
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: PUA - NPS Tunneling Tool Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of NPS, a port forwarding and intranet penetration proxy server
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - NSudo Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of NSudo tool for command execution
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: PUA - PingCastle Execution From Potentially Suspicious Parent
rules.description: Detects the execution of PingCastle, a tool designed to quickly assess the Active Directory security level via a script located in a potentially suspicious or uncommon location.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: 1 of selection_parent_* and selection_parent_ext and selection_cli

rules.title: PUA - PingCastle Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of PingCastle, a tool designed to quickly assess the Active Directory security level.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), frack113

rules.title: PUA - Process Hacker Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Process Hacker based on binary metadata information (Image, Hash, Imphash, etc).
Process Hacker is a tool to view and manipulate processes, kernel options and other low level options.
Threat actors abused older vulnerable versions to manipulate system processes.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: While sometimes 'Process Hacker is used by legitimate administrators, the execution of Process Hacker must be investigated and allowed on a case by case basis

rules.title: PUA - Radmin Viewer Utility Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of Radmin which can be abused by an adversary to remotely control Windows machines
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: PUA - Potential PE Metadata Tamper Using Rcedit
rules.description: Detects the use of rcedit to potentially alter executable PE metadata properties, which could conceal efforts to rename system utilities for defense evasion.
rules.author: Micah Babinski
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the tool by administrators or users to update metadata of a binary

rules.title: PUA - Rclone Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of RClone utility for exfiltration as used by various ransomwares strains like REvil, Conti, FiveHands, etc
rules.author: Bhabesh Raj, Sittikorn S, Aaron Greetham (@beardofbinary) - NCC Group

rules.title: PUA - Restic Backup Tool Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of the Restic backup tool, which can be used for data exfiltration.
Threat actors may leverage Restic to back up and exfiltrate sensitive data to remote storage locations, including cloud services.
If not legitimately used in the enterprise environment, its presence may indicate malicious activity.
rules.author: Nounou Mbeiri, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Restic for backup purposes within the organization.

rules.title: PUA - RunXCmd Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of the RunXCmd tool to execute commands with System or TrustedInstaller accounts
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - Seatbelt Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of the PUA/Recon tool Seatbelt via PE information of command line parameters
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - System Informer Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of System Informer, a task manager tool to view and manipulate processes, kernel options and other low level operations
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: System Informer is regularly used legitimately by system administrators or developers. Apply additional filters accordingly

rules.title: PUA - TruffleHog Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of TruffleHog, a tool used to search for secrets in different platforms like Git, Jira, Slack, SharePoint, etc. that could be used maliciously.
While it is a legitimate tool, intended for use in CI pipelines and security assessments,
It was observed in the Shai-Hulud malware campaign targeting npm packages to steal sensitive information.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of TruffleHog by security teams or developers.

rules.title: PUA - WebBrowserPassView Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of WebBrowserPassView.exe. A password recovery tool that reveals the passwords stored by the following Web browsers, Internet Explorer (Version 4.0 - 11.0), Mozilla Firefox (All Versions), Google Chrome, Safari, and Opera
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: PUA - Wsudo Suspicious Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of wsudo (Windows Sudo Utility). Which is a tool that let the user execute programs with different permissions (System, Trusted Installer, Administrator...etc)
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - Adidnsdump Execution
rules.description:
This tool enables enumeration and exporting of all DNS records in the zone for recon purposes of internal networks Python 3 and python.exe must be installed,
Usee to Query/modify DNS records for Active Directory integrated DNS via LDAP
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Python One-Liners with Base64 Decoding
rules.description:
Detects Python one-liners that use base64 decoding functions in command line executions.
Malicious scripts or attackers often use python one-liners to decode and execute base64-encoded payloads, which is a common technique for obfuscation and evasion.
rules.author: Hugh Ryan (HueCodes), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Python for decoding data, which is uncommon in typical enterprise environments but possible in development or data analysis contexts.

rules.title: Python Inline Command Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of python using the "-c" flag. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live python code.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Python libraries that use a flag starting with "-c". Filter according to your environment

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Python Spawning Pretty TTY on Windows
rules.description: Detects python spawning a pretty tty
rules.author: Nextron Systems

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Usage Of Qemu
rules.description:
Detects potentially suspicious execution of the Qemu utility in a Windows environment.
Threat actors have leveraged this utility and this technique for achieving network access as reported by Kaspersky.
rules.author: Muhammad Faisal (@faisalusuf), Hunter Juhan (@threatHNTR)

rules.title: Query Usage To Exfil Data
rules.description: Detects usage of "query.exe" a system binary to exfil information such as "sessions" and "processes" for later use
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: QuickAssist Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of Microsoft Quick Assist tool "QuickAssist.exe". This utility can be used by attackers to gain remote access.
rules.author: Muhammad Faisal (@faisalusuf)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Quick Assist in the environment.

rules.title: Files Added To An Archive Using Rar.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of "rar" to add files to an archive for potential compression. An adversary may compress data (e.g. sensitive documents) that is collected prior to exfiltration in order to make it portable and minimize the amount of data sent over the network.
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, E.M. Anhaus, oscd.community
falsepositives: Highly likely if rar is a default archiver in the monitored environment.

rules.title: Rar Usage with Password and Compression Level
rules.description: Detects the use of rar.exe, on the command line, to create an archive with password protection or with a specific compression level. This is pretty indicative of malicious actions.
rules.author: @ROxPinTeddy
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Winrar command line version
Other command line tools, that use these flags

rules.title: Suspicious Greedy Compression Using Rar.EXE
rules.description: Detects RAR usage that creates an archive from a suspicious folder, either a system folder or one of the folders often used by attackers for staging purposes
rules.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: 1 of selection_opt_* and all of selection_cli_*

rules.title: Suspicious RASdial Activity
rules.description: Detects suspicious process related to rasdial.exe
rules.author: juju4
falsepositives: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: RDP Enable or Disable via Win32_TerminalServiceSetting WMI Class
rules.description:
Detects enabling or disabling of Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) using alternate methods such as WMIC or PowerShell.
In PowerShell one-liner commands, the "SetAllowTSConnections" method of the "Win32_TerminalServiceSetting" class may be used to enable or disable RDP.
In WMIC, the "rdtoggle" alias or "Win32_TerminalServiceSetting" class may be used for the same purpose.
rules.author: Daniel Koifman (KoifSec), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate system administrators enabling RDP for remote support

rules.title: Process Memory Dump via RdrLeakDiag.EXE
rules.description: Detects the use of the Microsoft Windows Resource Leak Diagnostic tool "rdrleakdiag.exe" to dump process memory
rules.author: Cedric MAURUGEON, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Windows Recovery Environment Disabled Via Reagentc
rules.description:
Detects attempts to disable windows recovery environment using Reagentc.
ReAgentc.exe is a command-line tool in Windows used to manage the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE).
It allows users to enable, disable, and configure WinRE, which is used for troubleshooting and repairing common boot issues.
rules.author: Daniel Koifman (KoifSec), Michael Vilshin

rules.title: Potential Persistence Attempt Via Run Keys Using Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious command line reg.exe tool adding key to RUN key in Registry
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.

rules.title: Add SafeBoot Keys Via Reg Utility
rules.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "add" or "copy" flags on safe boot registry keys. Often used by attacker to allow the ransomware to work in safe mode as some security products do not
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Reg Add BitLocker
rules.description: Detects suspicious addition to BitLocker related registry keys via the reg.exe utility
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Dropping Of Password Filter DLL
rules.description: Detects dropping of dll files in system32 that may be used to retrieve user credentials from LSASS
rules.author: Sreeman

rules.title: Suspicious Windows Defender Folder Exclusion Added Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" to add Defender folder exclusions. Qbot has been seen using this technique to add exclusions for folders within AppData and ProgramData.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: RunMRU Registry Key Deletion
rules.description:
Detects deletion of the RunMRU registry key, which stores the history of commands executed via the Run dialog.
In the clickfix techniques, the phishing lures instruct users to open a run dialog through (Win + R) and execute malicious commands.
Adversaries may delete this key to cover their tracks after executing commands.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: SafeBoot Registry Key Deleted Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "delete" flag on safe boot registry keys. Often used by attacker to prevent safeboot execution of security products
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Tim Shelton

rules.title: Service Registry Key Deleted Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "delete" flag on services registry key. Often used by attacker to remove AV software services
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Desktop Background Change Using Reg.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "reg.exe" to alter registry keys that would replace the user's desktop background.
This is a common technique used by malware to change the desktop background to a ransom note or other image.
rules.author: Stephen Lincoln @slincoln-aiq (AttackIQ)
falsepositives: Administrative scripts that change the desktop background to a company logo or other image.

detection.condition: all of selection_reg_* and selection_keys and 1 of selection_cli_reg_*

rules.title: Direct Autorun Keys Modification
rules.description: Detects direct modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry using reg.exe.
rules.author: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.

rules.title: Disabling Windows Defender WMI Autologger Session via Reg.exe
rules.description:
Detects the use of reg.exe to disable the Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) Autologger session for Windows Defender API and Audit events.
By setting the 'Start' value to '0' for the 'DefenderApiLogger' or 'DefenderAuditLogger' session, an attacker can prevent these critical security events
from being logged, effectively blinding monitoring tools that rely on this data. This is a powerful defense evasion technique.
rules.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_main_*

rules.title: Security Service Disabled Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" to disable security services such as Windows Defender.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), John Lambert (idea), elhoim

rules.title: Dumping of Sensitive Hives Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" in order to dump sensitive registry hives. This includes SAM, SYSTEM and SECURITY hives.
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Endgame, JHasenbusch, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, frack113
falsepositives: Dumping hives for legitimate purpouse i.e. backup or forensic investigation

rules.title: Windows Recall Feature Enabled Via Reg.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the enabling of the Windows Recall feature via registry manipulation.
Windows Recall can be enabled by deleting the existing "DisableAIDataAnalysis" value, or setting it to 0.
Adversaries may enable Windows Recall as part of post-exploitation discovery and collection activities.
This rule assumes that Recall is already explicitly disabled on the host, and subsequently enabled by the adversary.
rules.author: Sajid Nawaz Khan

detection.condition: selection_img and selection_value and 1 of selection_action_*

rules.title: Enumeration for Credentials in Registry
rules.description:
Adversaries may search the Registry on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials.
The Windows Registry stores configuration information that can be used by the system or other programs.
Adversaries may query the Registry looking for credentials and passwords that have been stored for use by other programs or services
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Potential Suspicious Registry File Imported Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the import of '.reg' files from suspicious paths using the 'reg.exe' utility
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: RestrictedAdminMode Registry Value Tampering - ProcCreation
rules.description:
Detects changes to the "DisableRestrictedAdmin" registry value in order to disable or enable RestrictedAdmin mode.
RestrictedAdmin mode prevents the transmission of reusable credentials to the remote system to which you connect using Remote Desktop.
This prevents your credentials from being harvested during the initial connection process if the remote server has been compromise
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Suspicious Query of MachineGUID
rules.description: Use of reg to get MachineGuid information
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Modify Group Policy Settings
rules.description: Detect malicious GPO modifications can be used to implement many other malicious behaviors.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Enable LM Hash Storage - ProcCreation
rules.description:
Detects changes to the "NoLMHash" registry value in order to allow Windows to store LM Hashes.
By setting this registry value to "0" (DWORD), Windows will be allowed to store a LAN manager hash of your password in Active Directory and local SAM databases.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Configuration And Service Reconnaissance Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" in order to query reconnaissance information from the registry. Adversaries may interact with the Windows registry to gather information about credentials, the system, configuration, and installed software.
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community

rules.title: Potential Tampering With RDP Related Registry Keys Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of "reg.exe" for enabling/disabling the RDP service on the host by tampering with the 'CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server' values
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), @Kostastsale, TheDFIRReport

detection.condition: all of selection_main_* and 1 of selection_values_* and not 1 of filter_main_*

rules.title: Suspicious ScreenSave Change by Reg.exe
rules.description:
Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by user inactivity.
Screensavers are programs that execute after a configurable time of user inactivity and consist of Portable Executable (PE) files with a .scr file extension
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Changing Existing Service ImagePath Value Via Reg.EXE
rules.description:
Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking the Registry entries used by services.
Adversaries may use flaws in the permissions for registry to redirect from the originally specified executable to one that they control, in order to launch their own code at Service start.
Windows stores local service configuration information in the Registry under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Detected Windows Software Discovery
rules.description: Adversaries may attempt to enumerate software for a variety of reasons, such as figuring out what security measures are present or if the compromised system has a version of software that is vulnerable.
rules.author: Nikita Nazarov, oscd.community

rules.title: Reg Add Suspicious Paths
rules.description: Detects when an adversary uses the reg.exe utility to add or modify new keys or subkeys
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Rare legitimate add to registry via cli (to these locations)

rules.title: System Language Discovery via Reg.Exe
rules.description:
Detects the usage of Reg.Exe to query system language settings.
Attackers may discover the system language to determine the geographic location of victims, customize payloads for specific regions,
or avoid targeting certain locales to evade detection.
rules.author: Marco Pedrinazzi (@pedrinazziM) (InTheCyber)

rules.title: System Restore Registry Modification via CommandLine
rules.description: Detects system restore registry modification via command line, which can be used by adversaries to disable system restore on the computer.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Disabled Volume Snapshots
rules.description: Detects commands that temporarily turn off Volume Snapshots
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Windows Defender Registry Key Tampering Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" to tamper with different Windows Defender registry keys in order to disable some important features related to protection and detection
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Rare legitimate use by administrators to test software (should always be investigated)

detection.condition: all of selection_root_* and 1 of selection_dword_*

rules.title: Write Protect For Storage Disabled
rules.description:
Detects applications trying to modify the registry in order to disable any write-protect property for storage devices.
This could be a precursor to a ransomware attack and has been an observed technique used by cypherpunk group.
rules.author: Sreeman

rules.title: RegAsm.EXE Execution Without CommandLine Flags or Files
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "RegAsm.exe" without a commandline flag or file, which might indicate potential process injection activity.
Usually "RegAsm.exe" should point to a dedicated DLL file or call the help with the "/?" flag.
rules.author: frack113
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Regasm by developers.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Execution Of Regasm/Regsvcs With Uncommon Extension
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious execution of the Regasm/Regsvcs utilities with an uncommon extension.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Execution Of Regasm/Regsvcs From Uncommon Location
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious execution of the Regasm/Regsvcs utilities from a potentially suspicious location
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Exports Critical Registry Keys To a File
rules.description: Detects the export of a crital Registry key to a file.
rules.author: Oddvar Moe, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community
falsepositives: Dumping hives for legitimate purpouse i.e. backup or forensic investigation

rules.title: Exports Registry Key To a File
rules.description: Detects the export of the target Registry key to a file.
rules.author: Oddvar Moe, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not all of filter_*

rules.title: Imports Registry Key From an ADS
rules.description: Detects the import of a alternate datastream to the registry with regedit.exe.
rules.author: Oddvar Moe, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not filter

rules.title: Imports Registry Key From a File
rules.description: Detects the import of the specified file to the registry with regedit.exe.
rules.author: Oddvar Moe, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not all of filter_*

rules.title: Regedit as Trusted Installer
rules.description: Detects a regedit started with TrustedInstaller privileges or by ProcessHacker.exe
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Registry Modification From ADS Via Regini.EXE
rules.description: Detects the import of an alternate data stream with regini.exe, regini.exe can be used to modify registry keys.
rules.author: Eli Salem, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

rules.title: Registry Modification Via Regini.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of regini.exe which can be used to modify registry keys, the changes are imported from one or more text files.
rules.author: Eli Salem, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

rules.title: DLL Execution Via Register-cimprovider.exe
rules.description: Detects using register-cimprovider.exe to execute arbitrary dll file.
rules.author: Ivan Dyachkov, Yulia Fomina, oscd.community

rules.title: Enumeration for 3rd Party Creds From CLI
rules.description: Detects processes that query known 3rd party registry keys that holds credentials via commandline
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Registry Export of Third-Party Credentials
rules.description:
Detects the use of reg.exe to export registry paths associated with third-party credentials.
Credential stealers have been known to use this technique to extract sensitive information from the registry.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: IE ZoneMap Setting Downgraded To MyComputer Zone For HTTP Protocols Via CLI
rules.description: Detects changes to Internet Explorer's (IE / Windows Internet properties) ZoneMap configuration of the "HTTP" and "HTTPS" protocols to point to the "My Computer" zone. This allows downloaded files from the Internet to be granted the same level of trust as files stored locally.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Debugger Registration Cmdline
rules.description: Detects the registration of a debugger for a program that is available in the logon screen (sticky key backdoor).
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Jonhnathan Ribeiro

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Logon Scripts - CommandLine
rules.description: Detects the addition of a new LogonScript to the registry value "UserInitMprLogonScript" for potential persistence
rules.author: Tom Ueltschi (@c_APT_ure)
falsepositives: Legitimate addition of Logon Scripts via the command line by administrators or third party tools

rules.title: Potential Credential Dumping Attempt Using New NetworkProvider - CLI
rules.description: Detects when an attacker tries to add a new network provider in order to dump clear text credentials, similar to how the NPPSpy tool does it
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Other legitimate network providers used and not filtred in this rule

rules.title: Python Function Execution Security Warning Disabled In Excel
rules.description:
Detects changes to the registry value "PythonFunctionWarnings" that would prevent any warnings or alerts from showing when Python functions are about to be executed.
Threat actors could run malicious code through the new Microsoft Excel feature that allows Python to run within the spreadsheet.
rules.author: @Kostastsale

rules.title: Potential Privilege Escalation via Service Permissions Weakness
rules.description: Detect modification of services configuration (ImagePath, FailureCommand and ServiceDLL) in registry by processes with Medium integrity level
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov

rules.title: Potential Provisioning Registry Key Abuse For Binary Proxy Execution
rules.description: Detects potential abuse of the provisioning registry key for indirect command execution through "Provlaunch.exe".
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: Potential PowerShell Execution Policy Tampering - ProcCreation

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - Anydesk Execution From Suspicious Folder
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of AnyDesk from a non-standard folder

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - Potential MeshAgent Execution - Windows
rules.description:
Detects potential execution of MeshAgent which is a tool used for remote access.
Historical data shows that threat actors rename MeshAgent binary to evade detection.
Matching command lines with the '--meshServiceName' argument can indicate that the MeshAgent is being used for remote access.
rules.author: Norbert Jaśniewicz (AlphaSOC)

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - MeshAgent Command Execution via MeshCentral
rules.description:
Detects the use of MeshAgent to execute commands on the target host, particularly when threat actors might abuse it to execute commands directly.
MeshAgent can execute commands on the target host by leveraging win-console to obscure their activities and win-dispatcher to run malicious code through IPC with child processes.
rules.author: @Kostastsale
falsepositives: False positives can be found in environments using MeshAgent for remote management, analysis should prioritize the grandparent process, MeshAgent.exe, and scrutinize the resulting child processes triggered by any suspicious interactive commands directed at the target host.

rules.title: Suspicious ShellExec_RunDLL Call Via Ordinal
rules.description:
Detects suspicious call to the "ShellExec_RunDLL" exported function of SHELL32.DLL through the ordinal number to launch other commands.
Adversary might only use the ordinal number in order to bypass existing detection that alert on usage of ShellExec_RunDLL on CommandLine.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

detection.condition: all of selection_parent_* and 1 of selection_susp_*

rules.title: ShimCache Flush
rules.description: Detects actions that clear the local ShimCache and remove forensic evidence
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: ( selection1a and selection1b ) or ( selection2a and selection2b )

rules.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Activity Invoking Sys File
rules.description: Detects suspicious process related to rundll32 based on command line that includes a *.sys file as seen being used by UNC2452
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Rundll32.EXE Execution of UDL File
rules.description:
Detects the execution of rundll32.exe with the oledb32.dll library to open a UDL file.
Threat actors can abuse this technique as a phishing vector to capture authentication credentials or other sensitive data.
rules.author: @kostastsale
falsepositives: UDL files serve as a convenient and flexible tool for managing and testing database connections in various development and administrative scenarios.

rules.title: Rundll32 UNC Path Execution
rules.description: Detects rundll32 execution where the DLL is located on a remote location (share)
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Rundll32 Execution With Uncommon DLL Extension
rules.description: Detects the execution of rundll32 with a command line that doesn't contain a common extension
rules.author: Tim Shelton, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Yassine Oukessou

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Suspicious Workstation Locking via Rundll32
rules.description: Detects a suspicious call to the user32.dll function that locks the user workstation
rules.author: frack113
falsepositives: Scripts or links on the user desktop used to lock the workstation instead of Windows+L or the menu option

rules.title: WebDav Client Execution Via Rundll32.EXE
rules.description:
Detects "svchost.exe" spawning "rundll32.exe" with command arguments like "C:\windows\system32\davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie".
This could be an indicator of exfiltration or use of WebDav to launch code (hosted on a WebDav server).
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

rules.title: Suspicious WebDav Client Execution Via Rundll32.EXE
rules.description: Detects "svchost.exe" spawning "rundll32.exe" with command arguments like C:\windows\system32\davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie. This could be an indicator of exfiltration or use of WebDav to launch code (hosted on WebDav Server) or potentially a sign of exploitation of CVE-2023-23397
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Rundll32 Execution Without Parameters
rules.description: Detects rundll32 execution without parameters as observed when running Metasploit windows/smb/psexec exploit module
rules.author: Bartlomiej Czyz, Relativity
falsepositives: False positives may occur if a user called rundll32 from CLI with no options

rules.title: Run Once Task Execution as Configured in Registry
rules.description: This rule detects the execution of Run Once task as configured in the registry
rules.author: Avneet Singh @v3t0_, oscd.community, Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock (updated)

rules.title: Possible Privilege Escalation via Weak Service Permissions
rules.description: Detection of sc.exe utility spawning by user with Medium integrity level to change service ImagePath or FailureCommand
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov

rules.title: New Service Creation Using Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new service using the "sc.exe" utility.
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator or user creates a service for legitimate reasons.

rules.title: Service StartupType Change Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detect the use of "sc.exe" to change the startup type of a service to "disabled" or "demand"
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: False positives may occur with troubleshooting scripts

rules.title: New Kernel Driver Via SC.EXE
rules.description: Detects creation of a new service (kernel driver) with the type "kernel"
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Rare legitimate installation of kernel drivers via sc.exe

rules.title: Interesting Service Enumeration Via Sc.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the enumeration and query of interesting and in some cases sensitive services on the system via "sc.exe".
Attackers often try to enumerate the services currently running on a system in order to find different attack vectors.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: Allow Service Access Using Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious DACL modifications to allow access to a service from a suspicious trustee. This can be used to override access restrictions set by previous ACLs.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Deny Service Access Using Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious DACL modifications to deny access to a service that affects critical trustees. This can be used to hide services or make them unstoppable.
rules.author: Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Service DACL Abuse To Hide Services Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of the "sc.exe" utility adding a new service with special permission seen used by threat actors which makes the service hidden and unremovable.
rules.author: Andreas Hunkeler (@Karneades)

rules.title: Service Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detection of sc.exe utility adding a new service with special permission which hides that service.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Service Path Modification
rules.description: Detects service path modification via the "sc" binary to a suspicious command or path
rules.author: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Persistence Attempt Via Existing Service Tampering
rules.description: Detects the modification of an existing service in order to execute an arbitrary payload when the service is started or killed as a potential method for persistence.
rules.author: Sreeman

rules.title: Stop Windows Service Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects the stopping of a Windows service via the "sc.exe" utility
rules.author: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: There are many legitimate reasons to stop a service. This rule isn't looking for any suspicious behavior in particular. Filter legitimate activity accordingly

rules.title: Suspicious Schtasks Execution AppData Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of a schtask that executes a file from C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Modification Of Scheduled Tasks
rules.description:
Detects when an attacker tries to modify an already existing scheduled tasks to run from a suspicious location
Attackers can create a simple looking task in order to avoid detection on creation as it's often the most focused on
Instead they modify the task after creation to include their malicious payload
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation Involving Temp Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks that involves a temporary folder and runs only once
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Scheduled Task Creation Via Schtasks.EXE
rules.description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks by user accounts via the "schtasks" utility.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Scheduled Task Creation with Curl and PowerShell Execution Combo
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a scheduled task using schtasks.exe, potentially in combination with curl for downloading payloads and PowerShell for executing them.
This facilitates executing malicious payloads or connecting with C&C server persistently without dropping the malware sample on the host.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of schtasks for administrative purposes.
Automation scripts combining curl and PowerShell in controlled environments.

rules.title: Delete All Scheduled Tasks
rules.description: Detects the usage of schtasks with the delete flag and the asterisk symbol to delete all tasks from the schedule of the local computer, including tasks scheduled by other users.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Delete Important Scheduled Task
rules.description: Detects when adversaries stop services or processes by deleting their respective scheduled tasks in order to conduct data destructive activities
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Disable Important Scheduled Task
rules.description: Detects when adversaries stop services or processes by disabling their respective scheduled tasks in order to conduct data destructive activities
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), X__Junior

rules.title: Schedule Task Creation From Env Variable Or Potentially Suspicious Path Via Schtasks.EXE
rules.description: Detects Schtask creations that point to a suspicious folder or an environment variable often used by malware
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Benign scheduled tasks creations or executions that happen often during software installations
Software that uses the AppData folder and scheduled tasks to update the software in the AppData folders

detection.condition: ( all of selection_1_* or all of selection_2_* ) and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Schtasks From Suspicious Folders
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creations that have suspicious action command and folder combinations
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Name As GUID
rules.description: Detects creation of a scheduled task with a GUID like name
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate software naming their tasks as GUIDs

rules.title: Uncommon One Time Only Scheduled Task At 00:00
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creation events that include suspicious actions, and is run once at 00:00
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential SSH Tunnel Persistence Install Using A Scheduled Task
rules.description: Detects the creation of new scheduled tasks via commandline, using Schtasks.exe. This rule detects tasks creating that call OpenSSH, which may indicate the creation of reverse SSH tunnel to the attacker's server.
rules.author: Rory Duncan

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser
rules.description:
Detects manual execution of the "Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser" task via schtasks.
In order to trigger persistence stored in the "\AppCompatFlags\TelemetryController" registry key.
rules.author: Sreeman

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Powershell Search Order Hijacking - Task
rules.description: Detects suspicious powershell execution via a schedule task where the command ends with an suspicious flags to hide the powershell instance instead of executeing scripts or commands. This could be a sign of persistence via PowerShell "Get-Variable" technique as seen being used in Colibri Loader
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Scheduled Task Executing Encoded Payload from Registry
rules.description: Detects the creation of a schtask that potentially executes a base64 encoded payload stored in the Windows Registry using PowerShell.
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), @Kostastsale, TheDFIRReport, X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Scheduled Task Executing Payload from Registry
rules.description: Detects the creation of a schtasks that potentially executes a payload stored in the Windows Registry using PowerShell.
rules.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_*

rules.title: Suspicious Schtasks Schedule Type With High Privileges
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creations or modification to be run with high privileges on a suspicious schedule type
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Some installers were seen using this method of creation unfortunately. Filter them in your environment

rules.title: Suspicious Schtasks Schedule Types
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creations or modification on a suspicious schedule type
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate processes that run at logon. Filter according to your environment

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_*

rules.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation via Masqueraded XML File
rules.description: Detects the creation of a scheduled task using the "-XML" flag with a file without the '.xml' extension. This behavior could be indicative of potential defense evasion attempt during persistence
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel, Elastic (idea)

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Suspicious Command Patterns In Scheduled Task Creation
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creation using "schtasks" that contain potentially suspicious or uncommon commands
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Software installers that run from temporary folders and also install scheduled tasks are expected to generate some false positives

detection.condition: selection_schtasks and ( all of selection_pattern_* or selection_uncommon or all of selection_anomaly_* )

rules.title: Scheduled Task Creation Masquerading as System Processes
rules.description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks that involve system processes, which may indicate malicious actors masquerading as or abusing these processes to execute payloads or maintain persistence.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate system administration tasks scheduling trusted system processes.

rules.title: Schtasks Creation Or Modification With SYSTEM Privileges
rules.description: Detects the creation or update of a scheduled task to run with "NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM" privileges
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Script Event Consumer Spawning Process
rules.description: Detects a suspicious child process of Script Event Consumer (scrcons.exe).
rules.author: Sittikorn S

rules.title: Potential Shim Database Persistence via Sdbinst.EXE
rules.description:
Detects installation of a new shim using sdbinst.exe.
Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims
rules.author: Markus Neis

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Uncommon Extension Shim Database Installation Via Sdbinst.EXE
rules.description:
Detects installation of a potentially suspicious new shim with an uncommon extension using sdbinst.exe.
Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Sdclt Child Processes
rules.description: A General detection for sdclt spawning new processes. This could be an indicator of sdclt being used for bypass UAC techniques.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

rules.title: Sdiagnhost Calling Suspicious Child Process
rules.description: Detects sdiagnhost.exe calling a suspicious child process (e.g. used in exploits for Follina / CVE-2022-30190)
rules.author: Nextron Systems, @Kostastsale

rules.title: Potential Suspicious Activity Using SeCEdit
rules.description: Detects potential suspicious behaviour using secedit.exe. Such as exporting or modifying the security policy
rules.author: Janantha Marasinghe

rules.title: NodeJS Execution of JavaScript File
rules.description:
Detects execution of JavaScript or JSC files using NodeJs binary node.exe, that could be potentially suspicious.
Node.js is a popular open-source JavaScript runtime that runs code outside browsers and is widely used for both frontend and backend development.
Adversaries have been observed abusing Node.js to disguise malware as legitimate processes, evade security defenses, and maintain persistence within target systems.
Because Node.js is commonly used, this rule may generate false positives in some environments. However, if such activity is unusual in your environment, it is highly suspicious and warrants immediate investigation.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of node.exe to execute JavaScript or JSC files on your environment

rules.title: Suspicious Serv-U Process Pattern
rules.description: Detects a suspicious process pattern which could be a sign of an exploited Serv-U service
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate uses in which users or programs use the SSH service of Serv-U for remote command execution

rules.title: Uncommon Child Process Of Setres.EXE
rules.description:
Detects uncommon child process of Setres.EXE.
Setres.EXE is a Windows server only process and tool that can be used to set the screen resolution.
It can potentially be abused in order to launch any arbitrary file with a name containing the word "choice" from the current execution path.
rules.author: @gott_cyber, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential SPN Enumeration Via Setspn.EXE
rules.description: Detects service principal name (SPN) enumeration used for Kerberoasting
rules.author: Markus Neis, keepwatch

rules.title: Setup16.EXE Execution With Custom .Lst File
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "Setup16.EXE" and old installation utility with a custom ".lst" file.
These ".lst" file can contain references to external program that "Setup16.EXE" will execute.
Attackers and adversaries might leverage this as a living of the land utility.
rules.author: frack113
falsepositives: On modern Windows system, the "Setup16" utility is practically never used, hence false positive should be very rare.

rules.title: Indirect Command Execution via SFTP ProxyCommand
rules.description:
Detects the use of SFTP.exe to execute commands indirectly via ProxyCommand parameter.
Threat actors were seen leveraging this legitimate Windows binary to bypass security controls and execute arbitrary commands while evading detection.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of SFTP with proxy commands for administration or networking tasks

rules.title: Suspicious Execution of Shutdown
rules.description: Use of the commandline to shutdown or reboot windows
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Suspicious Execution of Shutdown to Log Out
rules.description: Detects the rare use of the command line tool shutdown to logoff a user
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Uncommon Sigverif.EXE Child Process
rules.description: Detects uncommon child processes spawning from "sigverif.exe", which could indicate potential abuse of the latter as a living of the land binary in order to proxy execution.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon Child Processes Of SndVol.exe
rules.description: Detects potentially uncommon child processes of SndVol.exe (the Windows volume mixer)
rules.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Audio Capture via SoundRecorder
rules.description: Detect attacker collecting audio via SoundRecorder application.
rules.author: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community
falsepositives: Legitimate audio capture by legitimate user.

rules.title: Suspicious Speech Runtime Binary Child Process
rules.description:
Detects suspicious Speech Runtime Binary Execution by monitoring its child processes.
Child processes spawned by SpeechRuntime.exe could indicate an attempt for lateral movement via COM & DCOM hijacking.
rules.author: andrewdanis

rules.title: Suspicious Splwow64 Without Params
rules.description: Detects suspicious Splwow64.exe process without any command line parameters
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Spool Service Child Process
rules.description: Detects suspicious print spool service (spoolsv.exe) child processes.
rules.author: Justin C. (@endisphotic), @dreadphones (detection), Thomas Patzke (Sigma rule)

detection.condition: spoolsv and ( suspicious_unrestricted or (suspicious_net and not suspicious_net_filter) or (suspicious_cmd and not suspicious_cmd_filter) or (suspicious_netsh and not suspicious_netsh_filter) or (suspicious_powershell and not suspicious_powershell_filter) or all of suspicious_rundll32_* )

rules.title: Veeam Backup Database Suspicious Query
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious SQL queries using SQLCmd targeting the Veeam backup databases in order to steal information.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: VeeamBackup Database Credentials Dump Via Sqlcmd.EXE
rules.description: Detects dump of credentials in VeeamBackup dbo
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: SQLite Chromium Profile Data DB Access
rules.description: Detect usage of the "sqlite" binary to query databases in Chromium-based browsers for potential data stealing.
rules.author: TropChaud

rules.title: SQLite Firefox Profile Data DB Access
rules.description: Detect usage of the "sqlite" binary to query databases in Firefox and other Gecko-based browsers for potential data stealing.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Arbitrary File Download Via Squirrel.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of the "Squirrel.exe" to download arbitrary files. This binary is part of multiple Electron based software installations (Slack, Teams, Discord, etc.)
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Karneades / Markus Neis, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community
falsepositives: Expected FP with some Electron based applications such as (1Clipboard, Beaker Browser, Caret, Discord, GitHub Desktop, etc.)

rules.title: Process Proxy Execution Via Squirrel.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of the "Squirrel.exe" binary to execute arbitrary processes. This binary is part of multiple Electron based software installations (Slack, Teams, Discord, etc.)
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Karneades / Markus Neis, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community
falsepositives: Expected FP with some Electron based applications such as (1Clipboard, Beaker Browser, Caret, Discord, GitHub Desktop, etc.)

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Port Forwarding Activity Via SSH.EXE
rules.description: Detects port forwarding activity via SSH.exe
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Administrative activity using a remote port forwarding to a local port

rules.title: Program Executed Using Proxy/Local Command Via SSH.EXE
rules.description: Detect usage of the "ssh.exe" binary as a proxy to launch other programs.
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: Potential RDP Tunneling Via SSH
rules.description: Execution of ssh.exe to perform data exfiltration and tunneling through RDP
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Amazon SSM Agent Hijacking
rules.description: Detects potential Amazon SSM agent hijack attempts as outlined in the Mitiga research report.
rules.author: Muhammad Faisal

rules.title: Execution via stordiag.exe
rules.description: Detects the use of stordiag.exe to execute schtasks.exe systeminfo.exe and fltmc.exe
rules.author: Austin Songer (@austinsonger)

rules.title: Start of NT Virtual DOS Machine
rules.description: Ntvdm.exe allows the execution of 16-bit Windows applications on 32-bit Windows operating systems, as well as the execution of both 16-bit and 32-bit DOS applications
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Abused Debug Privilege by Arbitrary Parent Processes
rules.description: Detection of unusual child processes by different system processes
rules.author: Semanur Guneysu @semanurtg, oscd.community

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not filter

rules.title: User Added to Local Administrators Group
rules.description: Detects addition of users to the local administrator group via "Net" or "Add-LocalGroupMember".
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: User Added To Highly Privileged Group
rules.description: Detects addition of users to highly privileged groups via "Net" or "Add-LocalGroupMember".
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Administrative activity that must be investigated

rules.title: User Added to Remote Desktop Users Group
rules.description: Detects addition of users to the local Remote Desktop Users group via "Net" or "Add-LocalGroupMember".
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Execute From Alternate Data Streams
rules.description: Detects execution from an Alternate Data Stream (ADS). Adversaries may use NTFS file attributes to hide their malicious data in order to evade detection
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Always Install Elevated Windows Installer
rules.description: Detects Windows Installer service (msiexec.exe) trying to install MSI packages with SYSTEM privilege
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Mangatas Tondang (rule), oscd.community

detection.condition: 1 of selection_image_* and selection_user and not 1 of filter_*

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Windows App Activity
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child process of applications launched from inside the WindowsApps directory. This could be a sign of a rogue ".appx" package installation/execution
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate packages that make use of external binaries such as Windows Terminal

detection.condition: selection_parent and 1 of selection_susp_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Arbitrary Shell Command Execution Via Settingcontent-Ms
rules.description: The .SettingContent-ms file type was introduced in Windows 10 and allows a user to create "shortcuts" to various Windows 10 setting pages. These files are simply XML and contain paths to various Windows 10 settings binaries.
rules.author: Sreeman

rules.title: Phishing Pattern ISO in Archive
rules.description: Detects cases in which an ISO files is opend within an archiver like 7Zip or Winrar, which is a sign of phishing as threat actors put small ISO files in archives as email attachments to bypass certain filters and protective measures (mark of web)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate cases in which archives contain ISO or IMG files and the user opens the archive and the image via clicking and not extraction

rules.title: Automated Collection Command Prompt
rules.description: Once established within a system or network, an adversary may use automated techniques for collecting internal data.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Bad Opsec Defaults Sacrificial Processes With Improper Arguments
rules.description:
Detects attackers using tooling with bad opsec defaults.
E.g. spawning a sacrificial process to inject a capability into the process without taking into account how the process is normally run.
One trivial example of this is using rundll32.exe without arguments as a sacrificial process (default in CS, now highlighted by c2lint), running WerFault without arguments (Kraken - credit am0nsec), and other examples.
rules.author: Oleg Kolesnikov @securonix invrep_de, oscd.community, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

detection.condition: 1 of selection_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Potential Suspicious Browser Launch From Document Reader Process
rules.description: Detects when a browser process or browser tab is launched from an application that handles document files such as Adobe, Microsoft Office, etc. And connects to a web application over http(s), this could indicate a possible phishing attempt.
rules.author: Joseph Kamau
falsepositives: Unlikely in most cases, further investigation should be done in the commandline of the browser process to determine the context of the URL accessed.

detection.condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

rules.title: Suspicious Child Process Created as System
rules.description: Detection of child processes spawned with SYSTEM privileges by parents with LOCAL SERVICE or NETWORK SERVICE accounts
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Roberto Rodriguez (@Cyb3rWard0g), Open Threat Research (OTR)

rules.title: Potential Commandline Obfuscation Using Escape Characters
rules.description: Detects potential commandline obfuscation using known escape characters
rules.author: juju4

rules.title: Potential CommandLine Obfuscation Using Unicode Characters From Suspicious Image
